signals.topic: FirecrawlScrapeBlock failures due to insufficient credits and internal server errors
signals.summary: The FirecrawlScrapeBlock fails with two distinct errors: (1) 'Payment Required: Insufficient credits' — users hit quota limits and cannot scrape web content without upgrading their Firecrawl plan, and (2) 'Internal Server Error: All scraping engines failed' — the scraping service itself is unavailable. Both errors block web scraping workflows that AutoGPT agents depend on for research tasks.
signals.review_reason: 两种不同的 Firecrawl 集成失败：① 额度耗尽导致 402，用户无法执行依赖网页抓取的研究任务；② 服务端引擎全部故障导致 500，Web 抓取完全不可用。两条 issue 均由 linear[bot] 自动创建，说明是真实运行中触发的错误，影响 agent 自主运行的关键工具链。

source_issues.title: BlockUnknownError: raised by FirecrawlScrapeBlock with message: Payment Required: Failed to scrape. Insufficient credits
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 402 Payment Required. Firecrawl returns 'Insufficient credits to perform this request'. User is blocked from scraping unless they upgrade their plan.

source_issues.title: BlockUnknownError: raised by FirecrawlScrapeBlock with message: Internal Server Error: All scraping engines failed
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error. Firecrawl reports 'All scraping engines failed to retrieve content from this URL'. The entire scraping pipeline is down.

signals.topic: Workspace image not rendering in first assistant message when tool calls are used
signals.summary: When the copilot generates an image via tool calls (e.g. DALL-E → bash_exec → write_workspace_file), the markdown image in the first assistant message does not render. The workspace:// URL is correctly resolved by the proxy, but Streamdown's handling of markdown images within long multi-part merged messages fails to display the image in the initial message. Users can work around by asking the agent to regenerate the image, but the original output is lost.
aliases: workspace image not showing in first message
copilot image render bug first message
signals.review_reason: 明确的用户体验问题：用户在 copilot 中通过工具调用生成图片时，第一条 assistant 消息中的图片无法渲染。已确认后端数据和代理 URL 正确，问题在于 Streamdown 对合并消息中 markdown 图片的处理逻辑。影响用户查看 AI 生成的可视化内容，属于关键功能可见性缺陷。

source_issues.title: fix(frontend): workspace image not rendering in first assistant message with tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Image does NOT render in first message when generated via tool calls. Ask 'can you show the image again?' — image renders correctly in next message. Refreshing page doesn't fix original message.

signals.topic: Agent Outputs panel only shows last output instead of all intermediate outputs during a run
signals.summary: The Agent Outputs panel only displays the final output for agents that output multiple times during a single run. Users expect to see all outputs of a run, not just the last one. This is critical for debugging multi-step autonomous agent runs.
aliases: agent outputs panel shows only final output
signals.review_reason: 明确的 UI 功能缺陷：Agent Outputs 面板仅显示最后一次输出，丢失了自主运行过程中的所有中间输出。对于需要调试多步骤 agent 任务的用户而言，中间输出是排查问题的关键证据。标记为 good first issue，说明维护者也确认此问题真实存在。

source_issues.title: Only The Last Output Shows in "Agent Outputs" Panel
source_issues.evidence: Issue reporter explicitly states the Agent Outputs panel only shows the final output for agents that output several times during a single run, and it should show all outputs of that run instead. Reproducible by running an agent with multiple intermediate outputs.

signals.topic: Self-hosted setup guide link is broken, blocking local deployment

source_issues.title: self hosted guide link is broken

signals.topic: VSCode extension fails to connect to tabby server over SSH remote development due to localhost mismatch
signals.summary: When using VSCode remote development over SSH, the tabby VSCode extension cannot connect to a tabby server running on the remote machine's localhost. The extension attempts to reach the local machine's localhost instead of the remote's localhost, causing a 'Connect to Server Failed' error with 'fetch failed'.
aliases: SSH remote development localhost connection failure
VSCode remote SSH tabby server connection fails
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point — it blocks a primary workflow (remote SSH development) by causing connection failure. The extension misroutes localhost:8080 requests to the local machine instead of the remote machine where the server actually runs, leaving the user with no code completion. While only 1 issue, the evidence is concrete (exact error, steps to reproduce) and the blocking nature is unambiguous.

signals.topic: Docker 部署环境下 Gateway 连接失败，用户无法正常使用控制面板
signals.summary: Docker 部署时无法连接到宿主机上的 OpenClaw Gateway，配置 GATEWAY_URL 后仍然报 'Gateway is not reachable'，导致控制面板主流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 直接关联（#90 是 #86 的根因分析文档改进请求），均为 Docker 部署时 Gateway 无法连接，导致控制面板完全无法正常使用，主流程阻断。诊断信息不清晰加剧了用户排查难度，用户需要反复尝试多种 URL 格式组合（wss://.../ws、wss://.../ 等），影响明显。

source_issues.title: docs: 改进 Docker Gateway 连接配置文档和诊断提示
source_issues.evidence: issue #86 用户的诊断信息和配置分析，提供了完整的根因分析，指出 URL 格式问题和诊断信息不够清晰；建议改进诊断页面在 Docker 环境下提供具体配置建议

signals.topic: Docker 部署时群聊头像文件缺失导致头像加载失败
signals.summary: Docker 部署环境下群聊界面中 agent 头像无法加载，显示资源加载异常；根因是 Dockerfile 中未执行头像生成步骤，导致 staff-avatars 目录为空。
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 均指向 Docker 部署时群聊头像加载失败这一明确功能缺陷。#89 提供了完整的根因分析（Dockerfile 缺少头像生成步骤），#87 则是用户遇到此问题后的求助（AI 自动修复失败），共同证明该问题反复出现且难以自行解决，对群聊核心功能造成显著体验下降。

source_issues.title: fix: Docker 部署时 hall-avatars 头像文件缺失导致群聊界面头像加载失败
source_issues.evidence: 详细根因分析：serveHallAvatarFile 函数从 runtime/exports/staff-avatars/ 读取头像，但 Dockerfile 只创建了空目录，缺少 npm run avatars:export 步骤，导致所有头像资源（coq.png, main.png 等）在容器中不存在

source_issues.title: 群聊界面UI显示有问题【未解决】
source_issues.evidence: 用户确认无法正确获取 agent 员工头像，表现为资源加载异常；尝试让 AI 自动修复但第一个问题（头像）始终无法解决，仅修复了第二个问题（暗色模式），说明此问题有明确的技术难度且影响用户体验

signals.topic: 持续监控模式通过高频 CLI 轮询占满 CPU 核心，导致设备发热和功耗增加
signals.summary: MONITOR_CONTINUOUS=true 模式下，控制面板通过反复调用 openclaw CLI 在空闲机器上持续占满一个 CPU 核心，在被动散热的机器上导致持续发热，电池设备上造成严重功耗损失。
signals.review_reason: 虽然仅 1 个 issue，但提供了详尽的根因分析（代码行号级别的分析 + ps 实测证据），明确指出任何按独立安装流程且未关闭 launchd agent 的用户都受影响（服务默认以 RunAtLoad=true + KeepAlive=true 运行）。CPU 持续满载导致发热和电池消耗是可量化的成本损失，且仪表盘界面无任何可见症状，用户无法感知此问题，属于静默型资源浪费，有明确成本影响。

source_issues.title: Continuous monitor mode pins CPU cores via tight-loop openclaw CLI polling
source_issues.evidence: 详细技术分析：MONITOR_CONTINUOUS=true 模式下，setInterval 无速率限制，每个 tick fan-out 出 ~6-12 次 CLI 调用，每次调用 ~0.5s Node 冷启动，导致 CPU 100-120% 持续占用；ps 输出显示多个 openclaw 子进程同时运行；任何启用 launchd agent 默认配置的安装都会触发此问题，影响所有 Mac 独立安装用户

signals.topic: 文档工作台文件浏览器点击目录条目时触发 EISDIR 错误
signals.summary: 在文档工作台（Document workbench）点击目录（非文件条目）时，后端对目录路径调用 readFile 导致抛出 EISDIR 错误，影响文件浏览核心功能正常使用。
aliases: File browser EISDIR error on directory click
signals.review_reason: 提供了完整的根因分析和复现步骤，readEditableFile 对目录路径调用 readFile 导致 EISDIR 是明确的功能缺陷，影响文档工作台文件浏览的核心功能，用户每次点击目录都会看到错误，体验显著下降。虽然 count=1，但问题有完整的技术分析支撑，根因清晰。

source_issues.title: 文件浏览器点击目录报错 EISDIR
source_issues.evidence: 提供了完整的复现步骤、期望行为、实际行为和根因分析：buildEditableFileEntry 理论上过滤了目录，但展开后的目录条目可能混入 nav items，导致点击时触发 readFile(dirPath) 而非读取文件；readEditableFile → safeReadTextFile → readFile() 在路径为目录时抛出 EISDIR；用户提供了具体 API 调用路径和错误信息，问题在多种路径下反复出现

signals.topic: Default DEV mode enables unauthenticated API access leading to unauthenticated RCE in production
signals.summary: Default ENV=DEV skips JWT verification on all API endpoints, granting full admin access without authentication, and combines with toolkit installation RCE for unauthenticated remote code execution
signals.review_reason: Two security issues form a direct exploit chain: default DEV mode skips all JWT auth on every API endpoint (including toolkit installation), which when combined with the toolkit installation RCE allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Production deployments using defaults are fully compromised with no user action required. This is a critical user-impacting vulnerability with active exploitation path, not a theoretical security note.

source_issues.title: [SECURITY] Authentication Bypass — Default DEV Mode Skips All JWT Verification (CWE-287, CVSS 9.1)
source_issues.evidence: Default ENV value is DEV, which completely skips JWT authentication. All API endpoints using check_auth are unprotected by default. In DEV mode, get_current_user() hardcodes email='super6@agi.com', granting full admin access to any unauthenticated request. Combined with RCE vulnerability in Issue #1513, this enables unauthenticated remote code execution.

source_issues.title: [SECURITY] Critical: Remote Code Execution via Malicious Toolkit Installation (CWE-94)
source_issues.evidence: Remote code execution via malicious toolkit installation (CWE-94). Chained with Issue #1517 auth bypass for unauthenticated RCE.

signals.topic: SSRF vulnerability in WebScraperTool — internal service access and credential exfiltration
signals.summary: WebScraperTool performs no URL validation, allowing LLM-driven prompt injection to issue requests to cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), exfiltrating AWS credentials and internal service tokens
aliases: server-side request forgery web scraper tool
signals.review_reason: SSRF with explicit PoC demonstrating AWS credential exfiltration via cloud metadata endpoint. Prompt-injected LLM agents can cause the server to silently make internal HTTP requests, leaking cloud service credentials and internal tokens. This is an active exploitation path, not theoretical — any user deploying WebScraperTool in a cloud environment is at risk of credential theft without any special attacker privilege beyond controlling the agent's task prompt.

source_issues.title: [SECURITY] Server-Side Request Forgery in WebScraperTool — No URL Validation (CWE-918, CVSS 7.5)
source_issues.evidence: WebScraperTool._execute() calls requests.get(url) with NO URL validation — no blocklist for internal IPs, no check for 169.254.169.254, no check for private IP ranges. An LLM agent directed by prompt injection can make the server issue HTTP requests to internal services (cloud metadata, internal APIs), exfiltrating credentials and sensitive data. PoC demonstrates exfiltration of AWS IAM credentials via 169.254.169.254.

signals.topic: 内置OpenClaw版本更新失败，无法使用新功能

signals.topic: Gemini client shared across threads causing intermittent SSL/TLS failures under concurrent load
signals.summary: Gemini.get_client() caches a single google.genai.Client on self.client. Under concurrent multi-threaded usage (4+ threads), requests share one transport and intermittently fail with SSL/TLS errors like DECRYPTION_FAILED_OR_BAD_RECORD_MAC and WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER, breaking the main agent invocation path.
signals.review_reason: Users running Agno agents with Gemini in concurrent/multi-threaded environments experience intermittent SSL/TLS failures that block the main invoke() path. The error is reproducible with specific concurrent conditions. While count=1, the impact is a main-flow blocking runtime failure (not cosmetic), making P1 appropriate.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Gemini client is shared across threads, causing intermittent SSL/TLS failures
source_issues.evidence: Gemini.get_client() reuses a single cached google.genai.Client across threads. Under concurrent load, this shared client intermittently fails with TLS errors (DECRYPTION_FAILED_OR_BAD_RECORD_MAC, WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER). Reproducible with 4+ concurrent ThreadPoolExecutor workers.

signals.topic: Workflow Condition else_steps silently skipped via HTTP/AgentOSClient with 'No steps executed' result
signals.summary: When calling a Workflow with Condition steps via HTTP request or AgentOSClient, the else_steps are never executed when the condition evaluates to False. The workflow completes with 'No steps executed' content, silently swallowing the intended else-branch logic. Direct execution works correctly but remote execution breaks the else path.
aliases: workflow else branch not executed over HTTP
Condition else_steps skipped via remote call
signals.review_reason: Users building production workflows with conditional branching experience silent failure of the else branch when accessed via HTTP or AgentOSClient. The workflow completes without error but produces 'No steps executed', meaning business logic is silently skipped. This is a main-flow workflow runtime bug that is not immediately obvious to debug.

source_issues.title: [Bug] else-steps in workflow is not run when calling via http request or agentosclient
source_issues.evidence: Condition step with else_steps=[Step(agent2)] produces 'No steps executed' content via HTTP/AgentOSClient when condition returns False. The ConditionExecutionCompleted event shows executed_steps=0 and empty step_results. Direct execution works fine; remote execution breaks the else path.

signals.topic: Qdrant hybrid search always requires FastEmbed BM25 even when embedder provides native sparse vectors
signals.summary: When using Qdrant with hybrid search and a custom embedder that natively supports sparse vectors (e.g. bge-m3), Agno still unconditionally instantiates FastEmbed BM25 encoder. This causes an ImportError if FastEmbed is not installed, and even when installed, mixes sparse vectors from different representation spaces, degrading retrieval quality.
aliases: BM25 sparse encoder not skipped for native sparse embedders
signals.review_reason: Users with custom embedders that already support sparse vectors are forced to install an unnecessary FastEmbed dependency, and hybrid search quality is degraded due to vector space mismatches. The ImportError blocks the vector search workflow entirely.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Qdrant hybrid search always instantiates BM25 sparse encoder even when embedder provides native sparse vectors
source_issues.evidence: ImportError raised when FastEmbed is not installed. Even when FastEmbed is installed, bge-m3 native sparse vectors are mixed with FastEmbed BM25 vectors from a different representation space, degrading hybrid search quality. User must implement duck typing workaround.

signals.topic: RemoteDb sort_order enum mismatch crashes multiple AgentOS router endpoints
signals.summary: Four AgentOS router files declare sort_order as Optional[SortOrder] but set the default to the raw string 'desc' instead of SortOrder.DESC. On FastAPI 0.109.2+, this causes an AttributeError crash when sort_order is omitted and the RemoteDb path is used, since the handler receives a plain str instead of a SortOrder enum.
aliases: SortOrder enum default string value crash
signals.review_reason: Users of AgentOS RemoteDb path with FastAPI 0.109.2+ experience route crashes (AttributeError) when accessing 4 different endpoints without passing sort_order. This blocks the session/eval/memory/knowledge retrieval workflow. While a single issue, it covers 4 endpoints with a clear and reproducible crash.

source_issues.title: [Bug] RemoteDb routes define sort_order with a raw string default instead of SortOrder.DESC
source_issues.evidence: Affected: /sessions, /evals, /memory, /knowledge/content endpoints. On FastAPI 0.109.2, omitting sort_order causes AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'value'. 4 router files affected with the same pattern.

signals.topic: File handle leaks in transcribe_audio and pickle utilities causing resource exhaustion
signals.summary: agno/tools/openai.py transcribe_audio() opens audio files without a with statement or explicit close(), and agno/utils/pickle.py pickle_object_to_file() and unpickle_object_from_file() also leave file handles open. On long-running agents with repeated tool calls, file descriptors accumulate and can cause 'Too many open files' OS errors, breaking the agent process.
signals.review_reason: Long-running agents that repeatedly use the transcribe_audio tool or pickle utilities accumulate file handles until the OS enforces the file descriptor limit, causing process crashes with 'Too many open files'. The issue has a clear root cause and fix, and impacts production deployments.

source_issues.title: [Bug] File handle leaks in openai.py and pickle.py — open() without with/close
source_issues.evidence: openai.py:90 opens audio_path without closing; pickle.py reads/writes without closing file handles. Accumulated leaks lead to 'Too many open files' OS error, especially impactful for transcribe_audio() called repeatedly.

signals.topic: Custom @ai-sdk/google and @ai-sdk/anthropic providers drop API key at runtime with custom baseURL, causing silent 401 auth failures
signals.summary: Both custom @ai-sdk/google and @ai-sdk/anthropic providers load correctly but drop the configured API key at runtime when a custom baseURL is used, resulting in 401 'You didn't provide an API key' errors with no user-facing error message.
signals.review_reason: Critical feature unavailable: custom proxy providers for both Google and Anthropic are completely unusable. Users cannot use third-party Gemini/Claude proxies they have configured, blocking their entire workflow.

source_issues.title: Custom @ai-sdk/google provider loads correctly but drops API key at runtime when using custom baseURL
source_issues.evidence: The configured options.apiKey does not make it into the final request correctly. Runtime request fails with 401 'You didn't provide an API key'. Control experiment with @ai-sdk/openai-compatible succeeds with same key, ruling out invalid key.

source_issues.title: Custom @ai-sdk/anthropic provider loads correctly but drops API key at runtime when using custom baseURL
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as 21738: runtime auth propagation problem where options.apiKey is dropped between config resolution and request creation. 401 error with same control experiment proving API key is valid.

signals.topic: SessionSummary repeatedly loads full session history on every assistant turn, causing TUI freeze and multi-GB RSS growth
signals.summary: SessionSummary.summarize() is unconditionally called on every assistant finish-step, loading the full message history each time. This creates a hot loop during multi-step agent execution that freezes the TUI and drives multi-GB RSS growth.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: TUI becomes completely unresponsive and process memory grows into multi-GB territory during normal multi-step agent execution. This is not an edge case - it directly prevents users from completing tool-using workflows.

source_issues.title: Bug: SessionSummary runs on every processor finish-step and repeatedly loads full session history
source_issues.evidence: Tool-using sessions can freeze the TUI and drive multi-GB RSS growth because SessionSummary.summarize(...) is invoked on every assistant finish-step, and summarize() loads the full session history every time. Live diagnostic shows: prompt loop re-entry is happening during normal multi-step execution, repeated full-history loads are coming from summary, and processor-side summary calls explain the count gap.

signals.topic: Subagent mode agents fail to spawn due to session ID validation error
signals.summary: When dispatching subagent mode agents, OpenCode throws a session ID validation error 'must start with ses', causing all subagent mode agents to fail to spawn entirely.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: subagent mode (parallel task dispatch) is completely non-functional. All users attempting to use subagent configs get immediate validation errors - this is not intermittent but a permanent block on the feature.

source_issues.title: Subagent dispatch fails with session ID validation error: must start with "ses"
source_issues.evidence: When dispatching subagent mode agents, OpenCode fails with session ID validation error: 'Invalid string: must start with ses'. This affects ALL subagent mode agents - subagents are never created, so built-in TUI subagent navigation has nothing to show.

signals.topic: MCP HTTP client Bun hardcoded ~5 minute fetch timeout causes -32000 connection errors for long-running tool handlers
signals.summary: Bun hardcodes a ~5 minute fetch timeout that ignores AbortSignal.timeout(), causing MCP tool handlers exceeding this duration to permanently fail with -32000 'Connection closed' errors and permanently lost tool results.
signals.review_reason: Significant cost loss and feature unavailability: any MCP tool requiring more than ~5 minutes (interactive prompts, build tools, approval workflows) permanently fails. Users lose tool results and see duplicate attempts in chat history.

source_issues.title: MCP HTTP client: Bun's hardcoded fetch timeout causes repeated retries and -32000 errors for long-running tool handlers
source_issues.evidence: Bun hardcodes a ~5 minute fetch timeout that ignores AbortSignal.timeout() values. For MCP tool handlers exceeding this (interactive prompts, long CI/CD tools), fetch aborts causing 'TimeoutError'. SDK interprets as connection failure -> -32000 'Connection closed'. Tool result is permanently lost and duplicate calls appear in chat log.

signals.topic: Shell/session interrupt regression in 1.4.2 leaves TUI stuck and shutdown timing out
signals.summary: In version 1.4.2, interrupting a long-running shell/session action leaves OpenCode stuck; Esc twice does not reliably interrupt, session remains busy/stuck, and TUI shutdown ends with 'worker shutdown failed'. Downgrading to 1.3.17 fixes it.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: TUI becomes unresponsive and cannot be cleanly interrupted or shut down. Regression introduced in 1.4.2 means users are stuck with broken behavior until they manually downgrade.

source_issues.title: Shell/session interrupt regression in 1.4.2 can leave TUI stuck and shutdown timing out
source_issues.evidence: On 1.4.2, interrupting a long-running shell/session action leaves OpenCode stuck instead of returning cleanly. Esc twice does not reliably interrupt, session remains busy/stuck, and TUI shutdown ends with 'worker shutdown failed'. Downgrading to 1.3.17 fixes it.

signals.topic: Streaming response 解析时遭遇 json.MarshalJSON 错误（max_tokens 中断 tool call 场景）
signals.summary: v1.26.0 中，当 streaming 响应因达到 max_tokens 限制而在 tool call 中断时，触发 json.RawMessage MarshalJSON 错误，导致流式输出流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: 流式输出是 SDK 核心场景，当 max_tokens 在 tool call 过程中触发时出现 JSON 解析错误，直接阻断主流程。用户明确指出该错误发生在关键 token 限制处，导致流式响应无法正常处理，属于主流程阻断性 bug。

source_issues.title: Streaming:  json: error calling MarshalJSON for type json.RawMessage: unexpected end of JSON input
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告 v1.26.0 中 streaming 场景在 max_tokens 中断 tool call 时触发 MarshalJSON 错误，导致流式流程失败。

signals.topic: SDK 测试在 i386 (32位) 架构上因整数溢出编译失败
signals.summary: 多个内部包的测试文件中使用了超出 32 位 int 范围的常量值（237628372683），导致在 i386 架构上编译失败，Debian 包维护者无法通过测试。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但 Debian 维护者在多架构场景下面临持续阻断：包测试在 i386 上完全无法通过编译，属于关键平台兼容性问题，对依赖该包进行多平台分发的用户有明确影响。

source_issues.title: Tests fail on i386 (32 bit)
source_issues.evidence: Debian 包维护者报告在 i386 架构上测试编译失败，多个测试文件（form_test.go, json_test.go, query_test.go）均因整数溢出无法编译，64 位架构正常。

signals.topic: Prompt caching completely broken when streaming mode is enabled — cache info is null and caching silently fails
signals.summary: When streaming=true, prompt caching does not work at all: cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens are null, meaning users pay full token costs for every request with no caching benefit. This is a direct monetary loss for any production workload using streaming.
aliases: caching not working with streaming enabled
signals.review_reason: Two independent users report the same symptom with concrete evidence. The issue blocks the streaming use case — one of the SDK's primary code paths — and causes silent cost leakage: no error is thrown, but users are charged for uncached tokens. This is a high-frequency production-impacting bug.

source_issues.title: Caching does not work or not return cache info when streaming is enabled
source_issues.evidence: HTTP mode returns cache_read and cache_write tokens correctly; stream mode shows null for both fields. User provides side-by-side screenshots proving the behavior difference.

source_issues.title: Caching does not work or not return cache info when streaming is enabled
source_issues.evidence: User provides explicit JSON payload: streaming=false returns cache_creation_input_tokens=0 and cache_read_input_tokens=1454; streaming=true returns null for both. Reported July 2025 with no resolution.

signals.topic: Custom skills in container parameter produce non-deterministic cache prefix, completely breaking prompt caching for multi-turn conversations with skills
signals.summary: When custom skills are passed in the container parameter, prompt caching fails on every repeat request: cache_read_input_tokens=0 even though the request content is identical. This forces users to either abandon custom skills or lose all caching benefits, resulting in significant token cost inflation.
aliases: skills container parameter non-deterministic cache prefix
signals.review_reason: Single issue but backed by precise instrumentation data showing the exact token-level failure. The root cause (server-side non-deterministic resolution of skills content) is identified and plausible. Impact is high: forces a trade-off between using skills (losing caching, paying full price) or dropping skills. This is a core functionality breakdown for beta skills users.

source_issues.title: Custom skills in container parameter break prompt caching — consistent skills list produces non-deterministic cache prefix
source_issues.evidence: User provides a structured comparison table showing that without skills, Turn 2 gets cache_hit=35301; with 8 custom skills, Turn 2 gets cache_read=0 and cache_write=37327 (full re-write). Both scenarios use identical input. Impact: any user with custom skills cannot use prompt caching at all in multi-turn conversations.

signals.topic: API rejects pause_turn response with web_search block when resubmitted — API's own validator contradicts its own documented behavior
signals.summary: When the API sends a pause_turn with an unpaired server_tool_use block (no web_search_tool_result), and the user resubmits that exact block as the docs instruct, the API returns 400 error saying the tool use lacks a corresponding result. The API produces a block, tells the user to send it back, then rejects it.
aliases: pause_turn resumption API rejects its own output
signals.review_reason: This is a logic inconsistency in the API itself: the documented behavior explicitly tells users to resubmit the paused response as-is, but the validator rejects that exact payload. The workaround abandons in-flight search state, breaking the pause_turn workflow for web_search. This is a main-flow failure for agentic use cases.

source_issues.title: pause_turn with web_search: docs say re-submit response as-is, but API returns 400 — are we missing something?
source_issues.evidence: User submits exact error: API returns 'messages.1: web_search tool use with id srvtoolu_01UkjByNZ6pFvVLGAjWnYBjt was found without a corresponding web_search_tool_result block' when resubmitting the identical content the API itself produced. Workaround strips server_tool_use blocks entirely, abandoning in-flight search state.

signals.topic: pdfplumber completely broken in code execution sandbox — charset_normalizer mypyc module missing on import
signals.summary: pdfplumber cannot be imported in the code_execution_20250825 sandbox due to a missing compiled C extension from the charset_normalizer package. The error occurs on the very first line (import pdfplumber), making the documented pre-installed package unusable.
aliases: charset_normalizer mypyc module missing code execution
signals.review_reason: Key PDF handling functionality in the code execution sandbox is completely broken at import time. pdfplumber is documented as pre-installed. Users relying on it for PDF text/table extraction hit immediate failure with no path to resolution except discovering an alternative library themselves.

source_issues.title: pdfplumber broken in code_execution sandbox — charset_normalizer mypyc module missing
source_issues.evidence: Error is ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '81d243bd2c585b0f4821__mypyc' on import pdfplumber inside the sandbox. User confirms the workaround is to use pypdf instead, indicating pdfplumber is fully non-functional.

signals.topic: SDK import time of 209ms+ creates cascading 300ms+ import overhead in downstream frameworks like langchain_anthropic
signals.summary: Importing the anthropic Python SDK takes 209ms even for a single type import, due to all types being eagerly loaded. This causes langchain_anthropic to incur 300ms+ of import overhead just to make a single HTTP call, which is a significant performance degradation for any application importing the SDK.
signals.review_reason: The import slowness is a measurable performance degradation affecting any application that depends on this SDK. The 209ms figure is objective and reproducible via importtime. While not blocking, it materially impacts cold-start latency in frameworks like langchain and represents poor developer experience for a widely-used HTTP client library. Counts as a user experience pain point.

source_issues.title: Slow imports
source_issues.evidence: User provides python3 -X importtime output showing 209ms total import time, with anthropic.lib.tools at 69ms and anthropic.types at 116ms being the main contributors. Downstream package langchain_anthropic takes 300ms+ on import due to this.

signals.topic: partialParse crashes MessageStream when model outputs invalid JSON escape sequences (e.g. PHP namespaces)
signals.summary: When the Claude model emits tool call JSON containing unescaped backslashes (such as PHP namespaces like `App\Http\Middleware`), the `partialParse` function in `_vendor/partial-json-parser/parser.{js,mjs}` throws 'Bad escaped character in JSON' and crashes the entire `MessageStream` streaming response. The `generate()` function reconstructs JSON from tokens without sanitizing invalid escape sequences, causing `JSON.parse()` to reject the output.
aliases: JSON parse crash on backslash characters
streaming response crash invalid escape sequences
partialParse throws on model output backslashes
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed runtime bug that crashes the main streaming response path when models output common programming constructs (PHP namespaces, Windows paths, regex patterns) containing backslashes. The crash is in `MessageStream` — a core streaming component — and causes complete response failure. Though count=1, the impact is a main flow blocker with a complete reproduction case, making it P1 rather than P2. Feature request issues are excluded per the exclusion rules.

source_issues.title: partialParse in _vendor/partial-json-parser crashes on invalid JSON escape sequences from model output
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with reproduction code. The `generate()` function in `parser.{js,mjs}` outputs string tokens verbatim without sanitizing invalid JSON escape sequences (e.g. `\H` from `App\Http`), causing `JSON.parse()` to throw. The crash occurs at line 501 in `MessageStream.mjs` during `input_json_delta` accumulation, killing the entire streaming response. Includes proposed fix (sanitize invalid escapes by doubling backslashes and wrapping `partialParse()` in try/catch).

signals.topic: ProcessError stderr exit_code stripped — subprocess failures produce generic unhelpful Exception with hard-coded placeholder string
signals.summary: When the Claude CLI subprocess exits non-zero, the original ProcessError with structured exit_code and stderr fields is destroyed across three files. stderr is hardcoded as the literal 'Check stderr output for details' never capturing actual CLI output. The exception is then flattened to str(), and finally re-raised as bare Exception, making isinstance(exc, ProcessError) always False and exit_code/stderr attributes inaccessible. This makes diagnosing any subprocess failure (permission denied, bad config, internal error) impossible in production and CI.
aliases: exception flattening destroys subprocess error context
stderr hardcoded placeholder string prevents debugging CLI failures
ProcessError type destroyed during error propagation
signals.review_reason: Main flow is blocked: when CLI subprocess fails (common in permission denied, bad config, invalid model alias scenarios), users get zero diagnostic information. The stderr field is a hardcoded literal string that is never the actual subprocess output, making it impossible to debug failures. The ProcessError type is destroyed so the documented except ProcessError pattern does not work. Two independent issues confirm the same triple-defect chain. This is not a low-frequency edge case — CLI failures are a routine occurrence and users have no programmatic way to get actual error details.

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: Provides full reproduction with code showing isinstance(exc, ProcessError) returns False, stderr is hardcoded literal, exit_code and stderr attributes are stripped. Cites #515, #282, #238 as closed variants of same root cause.

source_issues.title: Error context destroyed through exception flattening — CLI failures produce unhelpful 'Command failed with exit code 1'
source_issues.evidence: Documents 3-step destruction chain across subprocess_cli.py and query.py. Shows stderr='Check stderr output for details' is hardcoded, ProcessError flattened via str(e), bare Exception raised so consumer except ClaudeSDKError never fires. Provides 6 additional specific code locations with bare Exception usage.

signals.topic: setting_sources=[] silently ignored — Python truthiness check treats empty list as falsy, global settings always load
signals.summary: Passing setting_sources=[] in ClaudeAgentOptions is treated identically to setting_sources=None due to a truthiness check (if self._options.setting_sources:). The CLI flag is never passed, so all setting sources (user, project, local) load including account-level MCP integrations from claude.ai, contrary to the user's intent of disabling all sources.
aliases: empty list for setting_sources has no effect
signals.review_reason: The setting_sources=[] API contract is violated silently: users cannot disable all setting sources as documented. This is unexpected silent behavior that directly defeats the user's intent — account-level MCP integrations from claude.ai load even when explicitly suppressed. Two independent issues confirm the same root cause in the same file at the same line. The bug is a simple truthiness vs None check that was previously fixed for allowed_tools but not applied to setting_sources.

source_issues.title: setting_sources=[] (empty list) silently ignored — global settings always loaded
source_issues.evidence: Documents that [] is falsy in Python so the CLI flag is never set. Shows expected behavior is setting_sources=[] should pass --setting-sources '' to CLI. Workaround uses non-empty list. Closed with fix suggestion.

source_issues.title: setting_sources=[] silently ignored due to truthiness check in _build_command
source_issues.evidence: Same truthiness bug on same line. Compares to #634 (allowed_tools=[]) which was correctly fixed with is not None check. Shows the same class of bug recurred for setting_sources. Workaround of setting_sources=[''] noted.

signals.topic: receive_response() streams tool results as UserMessage causing agent infinite loops
signals.summary: MCP tool results delivered via receive_response() are typed as UserMessage containing ToolResultBlock, indistinguishable from real user messages without inspecting content blocks. The model sees the tool result as user input and responds to it, triggering another tool call, creating an infinite loop. Users resort to system prompt hacks, content validation, and per-turn rate limiting as workarounds.
aliases: tool result message type ambiguity causes agent loop
MCP tool results confused with user input
infinite loop from tool result UserMessage
signals.review_reason: Main flow is blocked: agents using MCP tools via receive_response() enter infinite loops. The model repeatedly calls the same tool because it cannot distinguish tool result messages from user input. This is a core usage scenario that fails catastrophically with no clean fix available from the consumer side — the workarounds (system prompt hacks, content validation, rate limiting) are fragile and add maintenance burden. This is not a low-frequency edge case as MCP tool integration is a primary SDK use case.

source_issues.title: receive_response() streams tool results as UserMessage, causing agent loops
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces agent loop pattern: tool result arrives as UserMessage, model interprets as requiring response, calls tool again. Shows message sequence of alternating AssistantMessage/tool calls and UserMessage/tool results indefinitely. Documents three separate defense-in-depth workarounds needed to partially mitigate.

signals.topic: Background task notification leaks into next receive_response() turn causing model to answer wrong question
signals.summary: When a background task (spawned via run_in_background=true) completes between turns, its TaskNotificationMessage leaks into the next receive_response() call. The model responds to the stale task notification instead of the new user query, producing nonsensical answers. Workarounds like client.stop_task() are unreliable and produce 'No task found' errors.
aliases: stale task notification appears in next turn
background task completion leaks to wrong conversation turn
signals.review_reason: Main flow is blocked in multi-turn applications: the model answers the wrong question (stale background task status) instead of the user's actual query. Users cannot build reliable conversational agents because each new query is contaminated by notifications from prior turns. The client.stop_task() workaround is unreliable. This directly breaks the primary multi-turn use case of SDK consumers building chat or agent applications.

source_issues.title: Background task notification leaks into next turn after receive_response()
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction showing Turn 2 receive_response() yields stale TaskNotificationMessage from Turn 1, causing model to respond 'The background task completed successfully...' instead of '2+2'. Documents client.stop_task() workaround is unreliable with 'No task found' errors. References #558 (Second query hangs after background Task) and anthropics/claude-code#21343.

signals.topic: Session resume silently creates new session instead of resuming with no error or warning
signals.summary: When attempting to resume a session with a valid resume parameter and an existing session file, the SDK silently creates a new session with a different session_id without logging any warning or raising an error. The is_resuming flag is True, the resume session_id is correct, but the returned session_id is different. Users lose conversation context with no indication of failure.
aliases: session resume silently fails with new session created
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss: users explicitly request session resume and the SDK creates a new session with zero indication of failure. Conversation context is silently discarded. This is particularly severe for production applications relying on session continuity (e.g., customer support bots, coding assistants). Users have no way to detect the failure programmatically — the is_resuming flag is True but the actual behavior is a new session. This is a complete violation of the resume contract.

source_issues.title: Session resume silently creates new session despite valid session file and correct parameters
source_issues.evidence: Full logs showing is_resuming=True, correct sdk_session_id passed to SessionManager, but SDK returns a new session_id with no warning. Verified session file exists and is valid (21KB JSONL). Documents impact: users lose conversation context unexpectedly, no detection mechanism available, silent failure prevents debugging.

signals.topic: Prompt cache prefix mismatch causes every-turn cache misses and unnecessary cost
signals.summary: SDK injects <system-reminder> blocks into user messages as array format, but strips them on replay in history. This byte-exact format change breaks Anthropic's prefix caching, forcing cache_create on entire message history every turn instead of cache_read. Measurable cost waste: ~$0.08/turn at Opus rates (~11K tokens recreated per turn).
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with concrete cost impact: every turn wastes ~$0.08 in unnecessary cache writes. Issue includes full technical root cause (format mismatch between send and replay), measurable evidence, and 3 proposed fixes. Closed issue with developer engagement, confirming the bug is real and understood.

source_issues.title: Prompt cache prefix mismatch: system-reminder injection/stripping changes user message format between turns
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug: SDK sends user message as array with system-reminders on Turn N, but replays as plain string on Turn N+1, breaking byte-exact prefix. Measurable impact: ~$0.08/turn wasted at Opus rates. Reproduced with PoC scripts showing cache_read=0 cache_create=5539 vs stable format cache_read=4117 cache_create=1369.

signals.topic: SDK users experience repeated cache invalidation with no clear workaround
signals.summary: Multiple users report that the SDK consistently invalidates prompt cache every turn, including the system prompt. Some users found HTTP proxy workarounds but cache still fails. This is a direct cost loss for production deployments relying on prompt caching.
signals.review_reason: User pain point with clear cost impact: cache invalidation every turn wastes API costs. Multiple confirmations in comments showing it's not an isolated case. Though labeled 'question', the evidence shows a genuine UX problem causing ongoing financial loss. Related to #269 but reported separately with distinct evidence.

source_issues.title: Am I the only one struggling with invalidated caches?
source_issues.evidence: User reports cache invalidation every turn including system prompt, costing significant money. HTTP proxy workaround only partially helps. 6 comments with multiple users confirming the same pattern. This is the same root cause as #269 but reported from the user cost-impact perspective.

signals.topic: Bun --compile build regression: tempfile.js missing from published package (SDK 0.2.96)
signals.summary: Upgrading from 0.2.91 to 0.2.96 breaks bun --compile because extractFromBunfs.js imports ./tempfile.js which is missing from the published npm package. This is a regression that blocks Tauri/bun compiled builds entirely. Only workaround is downgrading to 0.2.91.
signals.review_reason: Clear regression: build works on 0.2.91, completely broken on 0.2.96 with a specific, traceable root cause (missing file in published package). Blocks a specific deployment workflow (Tauri + bun compile). No SDK upgrade path for affected users.

source_issues.title: Regression in 0.2.96: bun --compile fails due to missing ./tempfile.js import target
source_issues.evidence: Regression introduced in 0.2.96 (0.2.91 works). Error: 'Could not resolve: "./tempfile.js"' in extractFromBunfs.js line 17. tempfile.js missing from package contents and files list. Blocks Tauri compiled builds with bun --compile. Only fix: rollback to 0.2.91.

signals.topic: Plugin initialization timeout: Control request timeout on initialize in SDK 0.1.45+ (regression from 0.1.44)
signals.summary: Plugin initialization via SDK query() times out after ~65 seconds during the control protocol initialization phase, starting from SDK 0.1.45. The hardcoded 65-second timeout in _send_control_request() is exceeded. Affects Windows 11 users with local plugins. Working on 0.1.44, broken on all versions 0.1.45 through 0.1.56.
signals.review_reason: Regression affecting all plugin users on SDK 0.1.45-0.1.56. Full stack trace confirms hardcoded timeout exceeded during control protocol init. No workaround: plugin functionality is completely broken for affected users. Clear version-bounded regression.

source_issues.title: Plugin initialization fails with "Control request timeout: initialize" error in claude-agent-sdk versions 0.1.45 and above
source_issues.evidence: Regression: works on 0.1.44, broken on 0.1.45 through 0.1.56. Full stack trace pointing to _send_control_request timeout in query.py. Hardcoded 65-second deadline exceeded. Reproduced on Windows 11 with local plugins. No partial workaround available.

signals.topic: ExitWorktree fails across query() calls with same session ID due to lost session state
signals.summary: Worktree created via EnterWorktree in one query() call cannot be exited via ExitWorktree in a subsequent query() call, even when the same session ID is used. The worktree session state is not persisted across separate query() calls. Forces manual cleanup via git worktree remove.
aliases: worktree state lost across query calls
session state not persisted between query() calls
signals.review_reason: Core session management bug: users expect worktrees to persist across query() calls with same session ID, which is the documented/expected behavior. Forces manual filesystem cleanup. Referenced commit confirms the root cause. Breaks a key git workflow.

source_issues.title: ExitWorktree claims "no active EnterWorktree session" if worktree created in earlier query()
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps provided with minimal repo. ExitWorktree errors 'no active EnterWorktree session to exit' even with same session ID. Related commit 5a75d29 confirms the bug: 'EnterWorktree state lost across query() calls'. Worktree persists on disk requiring manual cleanup.

signals.topic: Bedrock/AWS authentication regressions in v1.0.90+ breaking CI workflows in tag mode
signals.summary: v1.0.90 introduced a regression where Bedrock/SigV4 authentication fails in the action's tag mode. The Authorization header sends raw base64 instead of AWS4-HMAC-SHA256, and OIDC-assumed credentials are not forwarded to the Claude subprocess. Tag mode crashes immediately with a validateHeaders error while agent mode recovers. Three separate issues filed within 24 hours describe the same regression affecting enterprise AWS users.
aliases: Bedrock auth broken in tag mode
Bedrock credentials not forwarded in v1.0.90
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues (two P1, one P2) all describing Bedrock/AWS authentication breakage introduced in v1.0.90. This is a core deployment model (Bedrock) for enterprise users, completely broken in tag mode (issue_comment + @claude). Users must pin to v1.0.89 as workaround, blocking access to other fixes. Confirmed external repo impact (fanatics-gaming/fbg-guidelines-api) with production CI failures.

source_issues.title: Bedrock validateHeaders error in tag mode (issue_comment + @claude), agent mode works fine
source_issues.evidence: Tag mode crashes with validateHeaders error while agent mode succeeds with identical config. SDK uses streamInput/for await loop with exitError check causing immediate crash in tag mode. Same SDK version v0.2.92, same action version v1.0.91.

source_issues.title: v1.0.90 breaks Bedrock auth with OIDC-assumed AWS credentials
source_issues.evidence: v1.0.90 (released 2026-04-08 04:42 UTC) causes Authorization header to send raw base64 instead of AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 SigV4 format. OIDC-assumed credentials not forwarded to Claude subprocess. Affects fanatics-gaming/fbg-guidelines-api with 403 errors in production CI.

source_issues.title: Bedrock SigV4 authentication broken after v1.0.90 (Claude Code 2.1.96 / Agent SDK 0.2.96)
source_issues.evidence: Same regression as #1196. SDK initialization uses Anthropic({ apiKey }) instead of Bedrock client despite use_bedrock:true. Authorization header missing SigV4 signing parameters. Affects all Bedrock-authenticated workflows after v1 tag update.

signals.topic: GitHub token expires after ~1 hour causing 401 errors and complete loss of job results
signals.summary: GITHUB_TOKEN expires during long-running jobs (1+ hours). When the token expires, the action receives 401 from GitHub API even though Claude completed successfully. The branch was never created and all progress was lost.
signals.review_reason: User loses all work from a ~1-hour job due to GitHub token expiration with no recovery or refresh mechanism. The action completes Claude's work internally but cannot persist results back to GitHub. This is a critical data loss scenario for any long-running review or automation task, particularly painful given the time investment lost.

source_issues.title: 401 GitHub after 1 hour job, no branch no commits, no comment update
source_issues.evidence: After ~1 hour of running, GitHub API returns 401 Bad credentials. Job finished successfully but GitHub failed to authenticate. Branch was never created, no commits posted, no comment updated. All work from a 1-hour review session was completely lost.

signals.topic: max_turns configuration silently ignored — conversations always truncated at default 10 turns
signals.summary: The action's max_turns input is never passed through to the SDK. run.ts calls runClaude() without the maxTurns parameter despite parse-sdk-options.ts correctly parsing INPUT_MAX_TURNS. All runs silently hit the SDK's default limit of 10 turns regardless of user configuration.
signals.review_reason: Users explicitly configure max_turns expecting to control conversation length but the setting is silently ignored. All runs cap at 10 turns regardless of configuration. Complex code reviews commonly require more than 10 turns and will fail mid-review without clear indication that max_turns is the cause.

source_issues.title: max_turns is never passed to SDK in run.ts, defaults to 10
source_issues.evidence: run.ts never passes maxTurns to runClaude() despite ClaudeOptions type supporting it. parse-sdk-options.ts correctly parses INPUT_MAX_TURNS but the value is discarded. SDK enforces its own counter with default of 10 turns, ignoring CLI --max-turns argument. Users cannot control conversation length.

signals.topic: External MCP servers configured in allowedTools never connect at runtime
signals.summary: External MCP servers specified via --mcp-config are processed for tool allowlisting but the MCP server registration step ignores --mcp-config. Only the hardcoded github_comment server connects. Users see MCP tools (e.g. mcp__notion__*) in allowedTools but ToolSearch finds no matches, resulting in NOTION_MCP_UNAVAILABLE errors.
signals.review_reason: A key advertised feature (external MCP server support via --mcp-config) is completely broken. Users who correctly configure MCP tools in allowedTools get silent failures where tools appear in the allowlist but are unusable at runtime. This blocks Notion integrations, custom MCP servers, and other explicitly configured tool integrations without any clear error.

source_issues.title: External MCP servers (e.g. Notion) listed in allowedTools but never connected at runtime
source_issues.evidence: --mcp-config and --allowed-tools with mcp__notion__* are processed for tool allowlist but MCP server registration ignores --mcp-config. Only github_comment (hardcoded) connects. Notion MCP tools show in allowedTools but ToolSearch finds no matches. User gets NOTION_MCP_UNAVAILABLE despite correct configuration.

signals.topic: Action crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths (CLAUDE.md) are symlinks
signals.summary: Since v1.0.89, cpSync in restoreConfigFromBase crashes when any SENSITIVE_PATH (e.g. CLAUDE.md) is a symlink. It tries to recreate the symlink rather than copy file contents, failing because the parent directory doesn't exist. Common in monorepos using symlinks for config inheritance.
signals.review_reason: Action crashes during setup phase (restoreConfigFromBase) when any sensitive path is a symlink, causing complete CI failure. This is a common pattern in monorepos that use symlinks for configuration inheritance. Users must pin to v1.0.88 to work around, blocking access to newer fixes.

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: cpSync in restore-config.ts uses dereference:false by default, trying to recreate symlink at .claude-pr/ instead of copying file contents. Parent directory doesn't exist when symlink() called. Affects CLAUDE.md and other SENSITIVE_PATHS when they are symlinks. Introduced in #1174. Users must pin to v1.0.88 as workaround.

signals.topic: TUI completely freezes and becomes unresponsive during long agentic sessions at high message counts (250+) on Linux/NixOS
signals.summary: Event loop starvation from terminal resize ioctl loop + unbounded message deferring causes TUI to freeze completely. All keyboard input ignored; only recovery is kill from external terminal.
aliases: TUI input freeze at high message volume
signals.review_reason: This is a main workflow blocking issue. Users cannot interact with Claude Code at all during long agentic sessions — no keyboard input works, only kill from external terminal can recover. The freeze occurs predictably at ~250+ messages and is confirmed via syscall analysis to be caused by a terminal resize ioctl loop combined with unbounded message deferring and excessive config file writes. This completely blocks the primary use case of Claude Code for extended sessions.

source_issues.title: [BUG] TUI completely freezes input at high message counts (250+) — ioctl TIOCSWINSZ loop starves event loop on Linux/NixOS
source_issues.evidence: Debug logs show useDeferredValue messages climbing to 250+ with deferred count climbing unbounded. Frozen process syscall analysis confirms syscall 16 (ioctl TIOCSWINSZ) — the TUI renderer is stuck in a terminal resize loop. ~/.claude.json being atomically rewritten dozens of times per second (~every 5ms) adds further I/O pressure. All keyboard input ignored (Enter, Escape, Ctrl+C), only recovery is kill from another terminal. Root cause: event loop starvation from constant full-screen rewrites + unbounded message deferring + config file churn.

signals.topic: Active Max subscription not recognized during authentication — users blocked from using Claude Code despite paid plan
signals.summary: Max subscribers receive subscriptionType: null during auth, blocking login despite verified active subscription on claude.ai.
aliases: Max subscription not detected during login
subscriptionType null despite active Max plan
signals.review_reason: This is a main workflow blocking issue for paying customers. A user with an active, verified Max subscription cannot authenticate to Claude Code at all — the subscription is not recognized during the login flow. This means a paying customer is completely locked out of the product despite having a valid subscription. The issue has been reproduced multiple times with different troubleshooting attempts all failing, indicating a systemic authentication bug.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Active Max subscription not recognized — subscriptionType: null, cannot authenticate
source_issues.evidence: User has active Max subscription verified on claude.ai/settings/billing. After browser-based authentication completes successfully (email and orgId returned correctly), subscriptionType is null and Claude Code shows 'Claude Max or Pro is required to connect to Claude Code'. Multiple troubleshooting attempts failed: full logout, credential deletion from macOS Keychain, fresh login, upgrade to latest version. This is not an API key issue — the user is a direct-paid Max subscriber who cannot use the product at all.

signals.topic: Promotional Extra Usage credits displayed but inaccessible — users blocked while balance shows available funds
signals.summary: Anthropic-issued promotional credits show as available in billing UI but API enforcement blocks usage as if balance is $0, causing $100 in valid credits to be inaccessible.
aliases: promotional credits not honored by API
signals.review_reason: This causes clear cost loss and blocks usage of already-paid-for credits. The user has $100 of Anthropic-issued promotional credits that they cannot use despite the billing page showing them as available. This is a direct financial harm on top of whatever issue prompted the original goodwill compensation. The billing display and API enforcement are reading from different internal buckets, making promotional credits effectively useless while appearing valid in the UI.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Promotional Extra Usage credits show remaining balance but system blocks as if /usr/bin/bash — billing enforcement/display parity
source_issues.evidence: Anthropic issued $200 in Extra Usage credits as goodwill compensation. After using $100, the billing page at console.anthropic.com correctly displays $100 remaining balance. However, the system prompts to add a payment method and blocks further usage as if the balance is $0. Root cause hypothesis: promotional/goodwill credits and user-purchased credits are tracked in separate internal buckets. The API rate limiter checks the purchased credits bucket (empty), while the billing display shows the combined balance including promotional credits. $100 of valid Anthropic-issued credits are completely inaccessible.

signals.topic: Dispatch main conversation permanently offline — server-side relay issue prevents main thread access while individual Cowork tasks work
signals.summary: Dispatch main conversation shows 'desktop appears offline' permanently; individual Cowork tasks work fine but the primary conversation thread is inaccessible via server-side relay issue.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the main Dispatch conversation which is a core Cowork feature. While individual Cowork tasks work, the primary conversation thread is permanently inaccessible. This is a significant experience degradation for users relying on Dispatch for multi-device workflows. The issue references multiple previous instances of the same class of problem, indicating it is a recurring pattern rather than an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: Dispatch main conversation permanently offline despite working Cowork tasks
source_issues.evidence: Main Dispatch conversation shows 'This desktop appears offline' on mobile client even when prompting from desktop. Individual Cowork tasks work fine — only the main Dispatch conversation thread is affected. User tried all troubleshooting: restart app, restart computer, full logout/re-login on both devices, deleted bridge-state.json, toggled Dispatch off/on with hard refresh. User notes this appears to be the same class of server-side relay issue as #40179, #40958, #41429, #41703. The underlying system is functional but the main conversation's relay/session is broken server-side.

signals.topic: --append-system-prompt-file flag silently drops all preceding files when passed multiple times
signals.summary: Passing --append-system-prompt-file multiple times only honors the last file; all prior flags are silently discarded without warning or error.
aliases: CLI flag parser overwrites instead of appends
signals.review_reason: This causes workflow failure for users who rely on combining multiple system prompt files. The flag silently fails (no warning or error) making debugging difficult. Users with legitimate use cases for multiple context files lose critical context without any indication something went wrong. While there is a workaround (manually concatenating files), the expected behavior based on the flag name is not delivered.

source_issues.title: --append-system-prompt-file is not cumulative — only the last flag is honored
source_issues.evidence: When --append-system-prompt-file is passed multiple times, only the last file is appended to the system prompt. All preceding flags are silently discarded — no warning, no error. The flag name 'append' implies cumulative behavior. Reproduction confirms ctx1 then ctx2 only shows ctx2 content, and ctx2 then ctx1 only shows ctx1 content. User's internal session orchestrator (BrainMon) relies on passing multiple context files, which silently fails.

signals.topic: LLM-based grading function produces false positives due to substring matching bug
signals.summary: The `grade_completion` function in the test-and-evaluate LLM grading example uses `"correct" in grader_response.lower()` for result detection. Since "correct" is a substring of "incorrect", every grader output is incorrectly graded as correct, yielding 100% scores regardless of answer correctness. This directly breaks the evaluation pipeline for any user copying the example code.
aliases: incorrect grading results in documentation example
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user-impacting bug: the grading function is part of a documented example that users copy into their evaluation pipelines. The substring bug causes all answers to be graded correct (100% score) regardless of actual correctness, completely breaking the evaluation workflow. The issue provides complete reproduction steps and a concrete fix. Count=1 limits it to P1 (single repo, not P0 threshold of count>=3 with multi-repo evidence), but it clearly qualifies as a workflow failure with measurable wrong outputs, not a minor edge case.

source_issues.title: [BUG] False positive in LLM-based grading example
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps provided: with a wrong golden answer 'The capital of Japan is Madrid', the grader correctly identifies mismatch and outputs `<result>incorrect</result>`, but the substring check `'correct' in 'incorrect'` returns True, causing the function to return 'correct'. Result: 100% score even with wrong golden answers. Users copying this example code will get entirely wrong evaluation results.

signals.topic: security-guidance plugin blocks file writes via substring false positives on non-JS files
signals.summary: The security_reminder_hook uses bare substring matching for 8 of 9 rules with no file-type awareness, causing pervasive false positives across .md/.py/.yaml/.json files and blocking the first Write/Edit of every new file due to dedup logic (exit code 2). The exec( substring is the worst offender in Python codebases using SQLModel, making the plugin a net negative for Python/other-language projects.
aliases: security-guidance false positives on non-JS/TS files
security-reminder-hook fires on markdown and non-JS source files
signals.review_reason: Blocks first Write/Edit of every new file in affected projects due to dedup exit code 2. Affects all Python projects (and any non-JS project) using security-guidance. This is a high-frequency, high-impact usability bug that actively prevents users from writing code.

source_issues.title: Security Guidance: substring-based rules fire false positives on docs, configs, and non-JS source files
source_issues.evidence: Uses bare substring match (exec(, eval(, os.system, pickle, etc.) with no file-type gate. Every new file costs at least one blocked attempt (exit code 2 dedup logic). Python codebases using SQLModel.session.exec() are especially hard hit.

source_issues.title: security-guidance hook fires on non-JS projects with JS-specific remediation
source_issues.evidence: Hook fires on .md files containing exec( in prose, blocks writes to documentation. User disabled hook globally as workaround. JS-specific remediation advice shown for Python projects.

signals.topic: ralph-loop session isolation failure causes loop state to leak across unrelated sessions
signals.summary: When CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is unavailable in the Bash tool context, ralph-loop writes an empty session_id, causing the stop-hook isolation check to be skipped. A loop started in one session then intercepts all other sessions in the same project directory, leaking prompts and wasting conversation turns.
aliases: ralph-loop intercepts wrong sessions due to missing session_id
session isolation broken when CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is empty
signals.review_reason: Confirmed session state leak across unrelated sessions, causing hundreds of wasted conversation turns. This is a critical session isolation failure that directly wastes user time and potentially executes unintended commands in wrong sessions.

source_issues.title: bug(ralph-loop): session isolation fails when CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is empty
source_issues.evidence: Empty session_id is falsy in bash [[ -n ]] check, so isolation guard is skipped. A loop leaked into 2 unrelated sessions, causing hundreds of wasted conversation turns before being noticed.

signals.topic: Discord plugin bun server.ts orphaned on Windows after Claude Code session closes
signals.summary: On Windows, closing Claude Code leaves the Discord plugin's bun server.ts process running as an orphan. Claude Code only kills its direct child (bun run) but not the grandchild (bun server.ts), so the bot stays connected to Discord's WebSocket and reacts to messages but cannot send text replies.
aliases: Discord plugin bun process orphan on session close (Windows)
signals.review_reason: Orphaned Discord bot stays connected and sends misleading emoji reactions without being able to respond. This is a clear process lifecycle bug on Windows that causes user confusion and a degraded Discord experience. Reliable repro with no automatic resolution.

source_issues.title: Discord plugin: bun server.ts orphaned on Windows after Claude Code session closes
source_issues.evidence: stdio MCP server grandchild process not killed on session exit. Bot stays online reacting to messages but cannot send text replies — confusing UX for Discord users who message the bot.

signals.topic: ralph-loop shell command permission check blocks plugin from running entirely
signals.summary: The ralph-loop plugin fails to run with a shell command permission check error: 'This command requires approval' for the setup-ralph-loop.sh script pattern. This has been a recurring issue reported across issues #50, #67, #69, #91, with multiple fix attempts (#72, #98, #117, #151, #1314) that were never merged.
aliases: ralph-loop blocked by shell permission check pattern
ralph-loop setup script requires approval error
signals.review_reason: Despite count=1, this is P0 because the plugin is completely non-functional — it cannot run at all due to the permission check blocking its own setup script. Multiple prior fix PRs were never merged, indicating a persistent unaddressed blocker.

source_issues.title: (ralph-loop) Error: Shell command permission check failed for pattern
source_issues.evidence: Recurring issue across multiple GitHub issues (#50,67,69,91) with multiple attempted fixes (#72,98,117,151,#1314) never merged. The plugin cannot function at all due to permission check failing for its own setup script.

signals.topic: Plugin marketplace contains broken/unusable published plugins (e.g., serena)
signals.summary: The marketplace lists plugins that are not updated or maintained, making them unusable in their published form. The serena plugin has open issues going back 6 months and is completely unusable as presented, eroding trust in the marketplace's vetting process.
aliases: Marketplace plugins not maintained or broken
serena plugin unusable despite being published
signals.review_reason: Published marketplace plugins being non-functional misleads users into installing broken tools, degrading trust in the marketplace. While count=1, the category impact (plugin discovery ecosystem) makes it P1.

source_issues.title: Marketplace usefullness
source_issues.evidence: serena plugin has open issues going back 6 months and is described as unusable. User explicitly states marketplace usefulness is degrading due to lack of maintenance.

signals.topic: Windows: Claude Code VS Code extension fails to read CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH environment variable, blocking launch
signals.summary: The Claude Code VS Code extension on Windows fails to detect git-bash even when the CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH environment variable is correctly set at both Machine and User level, causing the extension to fail to launch with error 'Claude Code on Windows requires git-bash'. This is a main-flow blocking issue for Windows users.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking issue: the Claude Code VS Code extension completely fails to launch on Windows when CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH is set. The user provided exhaustive evidence that the environment variable is correctly configured (both Machine and User level, git-bash in PATH, works in VS Code terminal), yet the extension throws an error asking to set the same variable. This is a clear bug where the extension's environment variable detection logic is broken on Windows, preventing any use of the product.

source_issues.title: Claude Code for VS Code fails to read CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH on Windows
source_issues.evidence: User has correctly set CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH at both Machine and User level, git-bash is in PATH, yet extension throws error asking to set the same variable that is already configured. Extension logs show: 'Error spawning Claude (on channel xbhcbex4fj): Error: Claude Code on Windows requires git-bash'. This blocks the primary workflow on Windows.

signals.topic: LibreOffice PDF conversion fails intermittently in pptx skill with no retry mechanism
signals.summary: The pptx skill's `convert_to_images()` calls LibreOffice headless PDF conversion once with no retry logic. In Docker/containerized environments, this fails intermittently due to stale lock files, concurrent processes, or profile corruption. The error is opaque ("PDF conversion failed") with no diagnostic info, and there is no retry with lock-file cleanup, --norestore, timeout, or stderr capture.
aliases: LibreOffice PDF conversion fails intermittently with no retry
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow-blocking issue: the pptx-to-PDF conversion is a core step in pptx skill usage, and intermittent failures with no retry/retries means any automated pipeline using this skill will randomly break. The error is opaque (no diagnostic info) making debugging hard. Count=1 because this is the only issue on this topic in the dataset.

source_issues.title: pptx skill: LibreOffice PDF conversion fails intermittently with no retry
source_issues.evidence: LibreOffice PDF conversion in pptx skill fails intermittently in containerized environments with no retry. Error message is opaque ("PDF conversion failed") with no diagnostic info. No retry with lock-file cleanup, --norestore flag, timeout, or stderr capture.

signals.topic: Git LFS mismatch for shadcn-components.tar.gz causes `git pull --rebase` to fail when repo is used as a submodule
signals.summary: The file `skills/web-artifacts-builder/scripts/shadcn-components.tar.gz` was committed as a raw binary blob, but `.gitattributes` tracks `*.tar.gz` with the LFS filter. This causes a persistent dirty working tree. When this repo is used as a git submodule, `git pull --rebase` in the parent repo fails outright.
aliases: Git LFS mismatch for shadcn-components.tar.gz breaks submodule usage
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow blocker: `git pull --rebase` failure in a submodule makes the repo unusable as a dependency in parent repositories. This breaks automated CI/CD pipelines that rely on submodule updates. Count=1 because this is the only issue on this topic.

source_issues.title: Git LFS mismatch for shadcn-components.tar.gz breaks submodule usage
source_issues.evidence: File committed as raw blob but tracked in .gitattributes LFS filter, causing persistent dirty working tree. When repo is used as a submodule, `git pull --rebase` in parent repo fails.

signals.topic: document-skills and example-skills plugins install identical 17 skills, wasting ~50k tokens per invocation and polluting Claude Code context

aliases: document-skills and example-skills plugins install identical content, causing duplicate skills
signals.review_reason: This is a persistent cost and UX issue: 50k wasted tokens per invocation directly translates to increased API costs and degraded context quality. The duplicate skills actively pollute Claude Code's context window on every use. Count=1 because this is the only issue on this topic in the dataset.

source_issues.title: document-skills and example-skills plugins install identical content, causing duplicate skills

signals.summary: When adding a remote MCP extension with OAuth authentication (e.g., Attio) to Goose Desktop, the OAuth browser flow never opens. Goose detects that auth is required but fails to trigger the browser-based authentication, leaving the extension unusable.
signals.review_reason: User cannot connect remote MCP extensions that require OAuth, blocking extension ecosystem usage. Works in competing products (Claude, ChatGPT). Clear main flow failure with specific third-party MCP provider evidence.

source_issues.title: Remote MCP OAuth flow does not open browser for Attio streamable_http extension
source_issues.evidence: Attio MCP works in Claude and ChatGPT but Goose detects auth is required yet does not launch OAuth flow. User cannot use third-party remote MCP extensions that require OAuth authentication. The same MCP server works correctly in competing products.

signals.topic: Provider/model switching fails with 'Could not contact provider' and 'Failed to fetch' errors

signals.topic: Streaming responses timeout after 30s despite configurable timeout being set to 1200s
signals.summary: Long streaming responses fail with 'Stream decode error: Ollama stream stalled' after exactly 30 seconds, even when GOOSE_TIMEOUT or OLLAMA_TIMEOUT is set to 1200s. A hardcoded GOOSE_STREAM_TIMEOUT of 30s overrides user configuration.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for any long-running streaming response. Regression in v1.30.0 that makes the existing timeout configuration misleading — user expects 1200s timeout but stream dies at 30s, forcing workflow interruption and manual restart.

source_issues.title: Goose Stream Timeout after 30s even when setting timeout to 1200s
source_issues.evidence: GOOSE_TIMEOUT and OLLAMA_TIMEOUT only affect connection timeout, not streaming. Hardcoded GOOSE_STREAM_TIMEOUT of 30s causes 'Stream decode error: Ollama stream stalled' for long responses. Regression in v1.30.0. User workflow is interrupted and requires manual restart.

signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for enterprise users with GH Copilot licenses on GHEC. The provider is completely unusable for this legitimate enterprise use case. Clear cost loss for enterprise users who have Copilot licenses but cannot use them with Goose.

signals.topic: Frontend extension tools are invisible to server agent routes and call_tool returns 500
signals.summary: Frontend extensions added via /agent/add_extension are not listed in /agent/tools and direct calls to call_tool return HTTP 500. The extension add succeeds but the tool is completely non-functional when accessed via server routes.

source_issues.title: frontend extension tools are invisible to /agent/tools and /agent/call_tool returns 500
source_issues.evidence: Frontend extensions added via /agent/add_extension are not listed in /agent/tools and direct calls to call_tool return HTTP 500. The add succeeds but the tool is completely non-functional through server routes.

signals.topic: keys tool does not perform variable substitution, causing literal %variableName% to be typed instead of resolved values
signals.summary: The keys tool (used by the agent for keyboard operations) does not call substituteVariables() before typing, so %variableName% tokens are sent literally to the browser instead of being resolved to actual values. This breaks agent workflows whenever the agent clears an input field and types a variable value (Ctrl+A → Delete → type pattern), causing passwords and other sensitive variables to be leaked as literal strings.
aliases: variable substitution missing in keys tool
literal variable name typed instead of value
signals.review_reason: The keys tool failing to resolve variable substitution is a confirmed user workflow break. When the agent needs to clear an existing field and type a variable value (a common pattern), the substitution step is skipped, causing literal strings like '%token%' to be typed instead of resolved values. This leaks variable names (e.g., passwords) as literal text in input fields and breaks automation flows.

source_issues.title: keys tool does not perform variable substitution
source_issues.evidence: The keys tool sends raw value directly without calling substituteVariables(), while type tool correctly resolves variables. When the agent uses keys for the flow: keys(press, Ctrl+A) → keys(press, Delete) → keys(type, %token%), the literal string %token% is typed instead of my-secret-value.

signals.topic: Opening a PDF print modal causes CDP session to crash with TargetClosedError, blocking all subsequent CDP operations
signals.summary: When act() clicks a button that triggers window.print() and opens a browser print dialog, subsequent CDP operations fail with 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. All CDP debugging/monitoring operations become impossible after triggering the print modal.
aliases: CDP session broken by print dialog
signals.review_reason: Opening a print modal breaks all CDP session operations on the page, rendering the CDP debugging/monitoring layer completely unusable. This blocks any user workflow that needs to interact with the page programmatically after a print dialog is triggered, which is a significant functional gap in browser automation.

source_issues.title: Opening Print PDF Modal on a tab with stagehand causes CDPSession.send: Target page, context or browser has been closed
source_issues.evidence: Using act() to click a button that opens window.print() causes subsequent CDP operations (stagehand.page.send_cdp()) to throw 'CDPSession.send: Target page, context or browser has been closed' with TargetClosedError. All CDP operations on the page become impossible after the print modal is triggered.

signals.topic: act() with Anthropic models fails Zod validation because response is wrapped in $PARAMETER_NAME key
signals.summary: When using an Anthropic model (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-5) as the default model for act(), the AI response is wrapped in a $PARAMETER_NAME key instead of being returned at the top level. This causes Zod schema validation to fail with AI_NoObjectGeneratedError and blocks the entire act() workflow.
aliases: Anthropic model act() Zod validation failure
signals.review_reason: act() is a primary workflow API in stagehand. When using Anthropic models, it throws AI_NoObjectGeneratedError and completely blocks the automation workflow. This is a main-flow failure affecting a core API, even though only one issue was reported — the bug is clearly reproducible and documented with root cause.

source_issues.title: act() fails with Anthropic models: response wrapped in $PARAMETER_NAME key
source_issues.evidence: Using anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 as the model for act() causes the response to be wrapped in '$PARAMETER_NAME' key, making all required fields undefined at top level. Zod schema validation fails and throws AI_NoObjectGeneratedError. The issue does NOT occur with OpenAI models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1-mini), indicating a model-specific parsing bug.
