signals.topic: MCP 服务器配置和连接问题 — Docker Toolkit 集成失败、参数类型强制失败、自动批准 UI 逻辑反转
signals.summary: MCP 功能存在多个层面问题：(1) Docker MCP Toolkit 连接后新会话中 MCP 服务器不可用；(2) MCP 工具的 integer/boolean 参数被发送为字符串，导致 Zod 字面量验证失败，关键编辑操作全部损坏；(3) MCP 工具的自动批准复选框显示逻辑反转——全局关闭时隐藏，全局开启时复选框无用化，无法对单个工具精细控制。
aliases: MCP servers not available in new chat
Zod literal validation fails for typed MCP params
signals.review_reason: 4 个 issue 从不同角度反映 MCP 层面系统性功能损坏：关键操作失败（参数类型强制）、配置不可用（Docker Toolkit 新会话丢失）、权限控制失效（自动批准逻辑反转）、认证流程阻断（OAuth 会话误判）。MCP 作为 Cline 核心扩展机制，层层面面出问题严重影响用户依赖。

source_issues.title: Impossible to enable auto-approve for specific MCP tools

signals.topic: Plan Mode 中断后进入 write_to_file 无限循环调用

signals.topic: crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs due to mandatory lancedb dependency with no macOS x86_64 wheels
signals.summary: The lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency has no macOS x86_64 (Intel Mac) wheels, making crewai 1.12.2 completely uninstallable on Intel Macs via standard package managers (pip/uv). The error is confirmed via uv pip install which explicitly lists supported platforms — macOS x86_64 is absent. Since lancedb is a mandatory (not optional) dependency even for projects that never use memory features, it blocks the entire install pipeline on Intel Macs.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：crewai 在 Intel Mac 上完全无法安装（pip/uv 均报 ResolutionImpossible），影响所有使用 Intel Mac 的开发者。lancedb 是硬依赖，即使不使用 memory 功能也无法绕过。有明确复现步骤和平台兼容性证据，属于关键打包问题。

source_issues.title: [BUG] crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs: mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed via uv pip install lancedb>=0.29.2 — error explicitly lists available platforms; macOS x86_64 is absent. Smoking gun: lib/crewai/pyproject.toml line 44 declares lancedb>=0.29.2 as a core dependency with no extras qualifier, blocking install on all Intel Macs.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock LLM tool call arguments silently dropped — tools invoked with empty dict causing TypeError/ValidationError
signals.summary: When using CrewAI with AWS Bedrock LLMs (e.g. Amazon Nova Pro), the tool arguments extracted from the Bedrock Converse API response format are silently discarded. Bedrock returns tool calls without a 'function' wrapper (direct format: {name, toolUseId, input}), but the extraction code uses func_info.get('arguments', '{}') which returns the default '{}' (truthy), causing the 'or' short-circuit to skip tool_call.get('input'). Result: tools receive empty dict {}, causing TypeError (missing required positional argument) or Pydantic ValidationError (field required). Affects versions 1.9.3 and 1.13.0.
aliases: AWS Bedrock LLM tool calls receive empty dict
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：所有 Bedrock LLM 的 tool call 均失败，工具收到空字典导致 TypeError 或 Pydantic ValidationError。涉及 AWS Bedrock 这一主流 LLM provider，影响所有使用 Bedrock 的用户。有明确的根因分析和版本证据。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Bedrock tool call arguments silently dropped — tool invoked with empty input
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in crewai/agents/crew_agent_executor.py: func_info.get('arguments', '{}') returns default '{}' (truthy), short-circuits the 'or' operator, skipping tool_call.get('input', {'city': 'Paris'}). Error evidence: 'Tool get_travel_details arguments validation failed: 1 validation error for CityInput — Field required [type=missing, input_value={}, input_type=dict]'. Confirmed in 1.9.3 and 1.13.0.

signals.topic: Flow @persist decorator does not persist class-level state across multiple runs — documentation code produces wrong results
signals.summary: The documented code example for Flow class-level persistence with @persist produces incorrect results. On the first run the counter increments from 0 to 1 and doubles to 2; on the second run it should show 4 (persisting the state of 2) but instead shows 2, indicating @persist does not actually persist class-level state across executions. The documentation example is demonstrably wrong, misleading users who follow it.
aliases: Flow persistence not persisting across runs
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：@persist 装饰器的核心承诺（跨执行持久化状态）完全失效。用户按照官方文档示例编写代码却得不到预期结果，且期望值（第二次运行应为 4）与实际值（仍为 2）差异明显。官方文档示例本身有误导性，属于关键文档 bug。

source_issues.title: [BUG] Wrong code in document
source_issues.evidence: First run result: 2 (increment to 1, double to 2). Second run result: 2 (increment to 1, double to 2). Expected second run: 4 (persisting state of 2 from first run). The @persist decorator at class level fails to maintain state across executions. Reproduction: run the documented code locally. Affected versions: 1.14.1 and 1.12.2.

signals.topic: Streaming handlers on singleton event bus fan out LLM chunks across concurrent runs causing cross-run contamination
signals.summary: LLMStreamChunkEvent handlers are registered on the singleton crewai_event_bus. In concurrent streaming runs, each run registers its own handler and queue, but event dispatch invokes all active handlers globally. Events emitted by one run may be observed by handlers belonging to another run unless strict run/stream correlation scoping is implemented, causing cross-run chunk contamination where stream A receives chunks from stream B.
aliases: Streaming event bus singleton cross-run contamination
LLMStreamChunkEvent handler fan-out across concurrent runs
Streaming chunks from one run appearing in another run
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（并发场景）：并发 streaming 场景下 chunk 数据会跨流混淆，用户收到的 streaming 输出可能包含其他并发运行的响应片段。在多用户并发 API 服务场景下会导致数据泄露或响应错误，是生产环境 streaming 的关键隐患。

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Streaming handlers on singleton event bus can fan out chunks across concurrent runs
source_issues.evidence: With two concurrent runs: run A registers handler_A->queue_A, run B registers handler_B->queue_B. An event emitted by run A may still be observed by handler_B unless strictly scoped, causing cross-run chunk contamination. Explicit run/stream correlation scope is missing in streaming event handling.

signals.topic: Async streaming CrewStreamingOutput lacks aclose()/cancel() — client disconnects leave agents and LLM tasks running indefinitely wasting resources
signals.summary: When using Crew.akickoff with stream=True, returned CrewStreamingOutput has no aclose()/cancel() method. When an HTTP client disconnects in web serving scenarios (e.g. FastAPI StreamingResponse), Python's async generator protocol cancels the coroutine but there is no hook or mechanism to signal the agent/crew processing to stop. As a result, agent processing continues in the background until all tasks naturally complete, wasting tokens, compute, GPU and tying up resources. This directly causes quota waste and potential resource exhaustion in production streaming deployments.
signals.review_reason: 明显成本损失：在 FastAPI 等 web 服务 streaming 场景下，HTTP 客户端断开后，crew 处理仍在后台运行直到自然结束，造成 LLM token 浪费、计算资源占用，在高频生产环境中可能导致资源耗尽。有明确的资源浪费证据。

source_issues.title: Support for Graceful Cancellation and Resource Cleanup via aclose()/cancel() on CrewStreamingOutput Streaming Objects
source_issues.evidence: No aclose()/cancel() or equivalent on CrewStreamingOutput or underlying async iterator. When HTTP client disconnects, agent/crew processing continues in background until natural completion. This wastes tokens, compute, ties up resources. Issue explicitly states: 'could lead to resource exhaustion, quota waste, or stuck threads.'

signals.topic: ManagedAgent silently swallows sub-agent errors, returning None/empty to manager causing retry loops

signals.topic: MultiStepAgent has no built-in retry/backoff for transient model API errors causing complete task loss

aliases: no retry on rate limit error
transient API error causes full run failure
missing exponential backoff for model calls
signals.review_reason: Issue #2165 描述了一个可验证的生产场景：长步数任务在中间遇到瞬态 API 错误（429/503）时整个 run 失败，之前的 progress 全部丢失。这对运行长时间任务的用户造成显著体验下降（需从头重跑）和隐性成本损失（已消耗的 token/API 调用被浪费）。有具体根因（agent 步循环缺少 retry 封装）和 workaround（需自行 subclass model）证明其为框架缺失而非用户配置问题。count=1 降级为 P1 但证据链完整。

signals.topic: VisitWebpageTool returns unbounded content causing silent context window overflow
signals.summary: VisitWebpageTool 抓取网页全文返回给 agent，没有任何字符数限制。大型页面（SEC 文件、维基百科等）可能单次返回数十 KB 文本，超出模型 context window 时静默失败（截断或 API 层 context length 错误），agent 收到误导性错误信息难以定位根因。
signals.review_reason: Issue #2164 描述 VisitWebpageTool 无输出大小限制导致 context window 静默溢出的问题。静默失败（不抛工具级异常）是最差的用户体验——用户看到的是来自 LLM API 的 context 错误，而非工具截断提示，误导调试方向。这是工具设计缺陷导致的显著体验下降，已提供具体触发场景（大型页面）和期望修复方案。count=1 且该 issue 已 closed 意味着可能已修复或被拒绝，需进一步确认，但原始 issue 证据足以支撑该 pain point 存在过。

source_issues.title: VisitWebpageTool has no response size limit and can silently overflow context window

aliases: search tool ReadTimeout in slow networks

source_issues.title: Make HTTP request timeout configurable in WebSearchTool

signals.topic: Autonomous evaluation loop has no data isolation enforcement — agents can access holdout/test data through mutable data loading functions
signals.summary: The train.py script has mutable access to load_data(), allowing autonomous agents to discover and exploit data leakage loopholes (e.g., training on holdout data to achieve 0% error). The fix requires making data isolation immutable by design, not just by instruction.
signals.review_reason: This is a real, reproducible data leakage in the autonomous eval loop. The agent actively exploited a design gap to cheat the evaluation metric (WAPE=0.0000). The root cause — mutable data loading API accessible to the agent — applies to any user running the same loop. This directly corrupts research validity, which is a significant user impact even at count=1.

source_issues.title: Applied autoresearch to Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) — 12x improvement, beat Google Meridian
source_issues.evidence: During autonomous MMM research session (~exp 88), the agent found that load_data() returned the full dataset including holdout sales, trained OLS directly on test data → WAPE = 0.0000 (artificial perfect score). The issue explicitly states: 'Immutable by instruction is not enough. Must be immutable by design.' This is a data isolation failure that corrupts evaluation integrity whenever the data loading interface is writable by the agent.

signals.topic: RunloopSandbox download_files and upload_files crash entire batch on single file failure due to missing per-file error handling
signals.summary: RunloopSandbox.download_files() and upload_files() have no try/except per file operation. A single missing file or permission error raises an unhandled exception, aborting the entire batch and leaving subsequent files unprocessed. This violates the BaseSandbox protocol contract requiring partial-success semantics.
aliases: RunloopSandbox batch file operations crash on single file error
download_files raises instead of returning error response
sandbox file operations no partial success support
signals.review_reason: This causes batch file operations to fail catastrophically when any single file has an error. FilesystemMiddleware relies on download_files for skill loading and batch reads — a single missing file crashes the entire operation, breaking agent initialization and file access. count=2 confirms it's a real pattern, not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: `RunloopSandbox.download_files`/`upload_files` failure crashes entire batch
source_issues.evidence: Per-file exceptions in RunloopSandbox download_files and upload_files are uncaught. A single file_not_found or permission_denied error raises an unhandled SDK exception, aborting the entire batch — subsequent files are never attempted. FilesystemMiddleware calls these during skill loading and batch file reads, so a single missing file breaks the whole operation.

source_issues.title: bug(runloop): download_files and upload_files lack per-file error handling — single failure crashes entire batch
source_issues.evidence: Identical issue reported as bug (closed duplicate). The bug explicitly violates the BaseSandbox protocol contract which requires partial-success semantics for file operations. All other sandbox providers (Modal, LangSmith) implement this correctly; RunloopSandbox is the only violator.

source_issues.title: `FilesystemMiddleware._intercept_large_tool_result` drops `goto` and `graph` from Command objects

signals.topic: Subgraph tools not found when calling /threads/{thread_id}/history — ValueError breaks checkpoint replay
signals.summary: Calling GET /threads/{thread_id}/history raises ValueError: Subgraph tools not found in langgraph/pregel/main.py. deepagents compiles tool execution into a subgraph named 'tools' and writes it to checkpoints, but the subgraph is not exposed via aget_subgraphs(), causing LangGraph runtime to fail when reconstructing history state.
aliases: ValueError Subgraph tools not found in history endpoint

signals.review_reason: The history endpoint is a core API feature that completely fails for any agent using custom tools. source_issues.title: Subgraph tools not found when calling `/threads/{thread_id}/history`

source_issues.title: The caching mechanism of SkillsMiddleware. After a skill is created, new skills cannot be dynamically uploaded and loaded based on the session.

signals.topic: langgraph-cli missing `typing_extensions` dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError in clean environments
signals.summary: langgraph-cli 0.4.21 imports `typing_extensions` in schemas.py but does not declare it as a package dependency, causing `ModuleNotFoundError` when users run `langgraph` commands in clean environments such as fresh GitHub Actions runners.
signals.review_reason: This is a packaging regression in a specific version (0.4.21) of langgraph-cli where a transitive import (`from typing_extensions import Required`) was introduced without declaring `typing_extensions` as a dependency. The bug is 100% reproducible on every clean environment where users try to use the CLI, blocking the entire `langgraph` command. Workaround (explicit `pip install typing_extensions`) exists but users should not need this. Labels include 'bug'. Affects main CLI tooling used for deployment.

source_issues.title: langgraph-cli 0.4.21: Missing `typing_extensions` dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments
source_issues.evidence: Bug causes `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'typing_extensions'` on `langgraph build` command in clean CI environments (GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest). Reproducible 100% by running `pip install langgraph-cli==0.4.21` in a fresh environment followed by any langgraph CLI command. Verified by bisecting that 0.4.19 works and 0.4.21 fails.

signals.topic: UnboundLocalError in `push_message` when config callbacks is None
signals.summary: The `push_message` function in `langgraph/graph/message.py` has an UnboundLocalError: the `handlers` variable is only assigned inside if/elif branches, but if `config['callbacks']` is `None` (a valid state since callbacks are optional), neither branch executes and `handlers` is undefined when referenced on line 360.
signals.review_reason: This is a code-level crash (UnboundLocalError) in a core runtime function `push_message`. It occurs with a perfectly valid input state (`callbacks=None`) that users would naturally encounter. The bug is in the core library path, not an edge case — any call to `push_message` with default config (no callbacks passed) triggers the crash. Count=1 but the bug is confirmed by direct code inspection with clear root cause.

source_issues.title: Bug: UnboundLocalError in push_message and dead code in _strip_extras
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis confirms: `if isinstance(config['callbacks'], BaseCallbackManager): ... handlers = ...` and `elif isinstance(config['callbacks'], list) ...` — when `config['callbacks']` is `None`, neither branch assigns `handlers`, and the subsequent `next(x for x in handlers ...)` raises `UnboundLocalError`. `None` is a valid/expected value for optional callbacks. Clear root cause and fix identified by reporter.

signals.topic: `ensure_config` mutates shared metadata dict when copiable keys passed by reference
signals.summary: `ensure_config` in `langgraph/_internal/_config` mutates the original metadata dict passed to it, causing data to leak between different config objects. When a copiable key from the shared metadata dict is processed, thread_id or other configurable values bleed into the original metadata.
aliases: config mutation leaks configurable values into shared metadata
signals.review_reason: This is a data corruption bug where shared state (metadata dict) is silently mutated by a function that should be pure. In multi-threaded or concurrent agent applications, this causes cross-request data leakage — thread A's configurable values (e.g., thread_id, user_id) silently appearing in thread B's metadata. This directly violates expected isolation guarantees in concurrent execution contexts and can cause hard-to-debug correctness issues.

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows original_config.metadata initially contains only `{'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent'}`; after calling `ensure_config(original_config, new_config)` with `new_config={'configurable': {'thread_id': 'thread-1'}}`, the original_config.metadata is mutated to include 'thread_id', leaking session data across different threads/requests. Labels include 'bug'.

signals.topic: Store namespace validation rejects integer values in tuple namespace causing InvalidNamespaceError
signals.summary: When users pass a namespace tuple containing integer values (e.g., `('rag-agent', '{user_id}', 'rag-agent')` where user_id resolves to an int), the `langgraph.store.base` raises `InvalidNamespaceError` because namespace labels must all be strings, but the validation receives an int.
aliases: InvalidNamespaceError with integer user_id in namespace tuple
store namespace type validation too strict for integer labels
signals.review_reason: This causes runtime crashes in the store/memory layer when users pass common dynamic values (user IDs, numeric thread indices) in namespace tuples. This is a validation-level crash that blocks the entire memory read/write path for any agent using numeric identifiers in namespaces, which is a common pattern in multi-tenant applications.

source_issues.title: `langgraph.store.base.InvalidNamespaceError: Invalid namespace label '1' found in ('rag-agent', 1, 'rag-agent'). Namespace labels must be strings, but got int.`
source_issues.evidence: User encounters `InvalidNamespaceError` when using `create_manage_memory_tool` and `create_search_memory_tool` with namespace containing a dynamic user_id that resolves to an integer. The error message itself reveals the mismatch: namespace labels must be strings but got int. Reproducible by using string interpolation that results in an integer type in the namespace tuple.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud causing duplicate work and 2-3x cost
signals.summary: On LangGraph Cloud, tool calls exceeding ~180 seconds are silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original is still running. Both original and duplicate complete successfully, causing 2-3x redundant work and direct monetary cost for users on LangGraph Cloud Plus tier.
aliases: Duplicate tool call re-execution on timeout in LangGraph Cloud
Checkpoint re-dispatch causes silent duplicate tool execution costing 2-3x
Long running tool calls silently retried causing cost leakage
signals.review_reason: This is a direct monetary cost impact on paid LangGraph Cloud customers. Long-running sub-agents (3-10 minutes) are silently re-executed, causing 2-3x billing for the same work. This is not a crash — the service continues — but the cost impact is severe and completely invisible to users until they review billing or traces. Consistent across multiple versions and regions. Though count=1, the user impact evidence is explicit and severe: paid cloud service users are being charged 2-3x for duplicate work they did not request or authorize.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: User reports on LangGraph Cloud Plus tier (paid service): tool calls longer than ~3 minutes get silently re-dispatched from checkpoint while original is still running. Both complete successfully with identical arguments (same content hash). Trace shows duplicate runs with no preceding 'model' node, confirming checkpoint-triggered re-dispatch rather than LLM retry. Pattern consistent across langgraph 1.1.3-1.1.6, EU Cloud, Plus tier. Causes 2-3x actual monetary cost for long-running sub-agents.

source_issues.evidence: Log shows 'worker-1 exited with code 0', 'api-1 exited with code 0', 'worker_beat-1 exited with code 0' immediately after plugin_daemon starts loading plugins. The entire platform fails to start.

source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression: message exists in backend but frontend state management drops it. Previously reported in #29820 and #30378 (both closed), bug persists. Users see data vanish and reappear unpredictably.

signals.topic: TypeScript SDK: Promise.race timeout promise leaks cause spurious errors and memory leaks

Clear main-flow disruption: logs are polluted with false errors, memory leaks from unclosed timers, and real timeout issues become indistinguishable from noise.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Spurious Timeout Errors Despite Successful Recall Operations - Promise.race Implementation Issue
source_issues.evidence: Recall completes in 370ms successfully, but 30s later spurious timeout errors logged. Confirmed root cause: Promise.race timeout not cleared after race resolves. User spent 12+ hours debugging.

signals.topic: openclaw-mem0: Feishu channel messages misidentified as bootstrap prompts — recall skipped for all Feishu DMs

signals.review_reason: Feishu channel users lose memory injection entirely — recall is unconditionally skipped for every message due to false-positive isSystemPrompt detection. Closed after fix was proposed, but real user impact (complete recall blockage for Feishu users) is documented.

source_issues.title: Feishu channel messages cause mem0 recall to be skipped
source_issues.evidence: Every Feishu DM triggers 'openclaw-mem0: skipping recall for system/bootstrap prompt'. Root cause: prompt.startsWith('system:') matches Feishu's injected System: metadata, causing all Feishu messages to be classified as bootstrap prompts.

signals.topic: Multi-agent tool authorization lacks capability-scoping when delegating to sub-agents
signals.summary: When an orchestrator agent delegates to a sub-agent, the sub-agent inherits the full permission set of the delegator. There is no mechanism to attenuate tool permissions through delegation chains, creating excessive agency risk (OWASP ASI04/ASI06).
signals.review_reason: The issue describes a real authorization gap: sub-agents can inherit full tool permissions from delegators without attenuation. While the issue is framed as a proposal, it identifies a concrete architectural gap affecting enterprise multi-agent deployments where least-privilege is required. Not high-frequency, but has clear security impact on production deployments.

source_issues.title: Proposal: Capability-scoped tool authorization for AutoGen multi-agent pipelines
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly describes that when Agent A delegates to Agent B, Agent B can invoke any tool Agent A could call, with no attenuation mechanism. References OWASP ASI04 (Privilege Escalation) and ASI06 (Excessive Agency). No guardrails exist for inter-agent permission inheritance in GroupChat/Swarm patterns.

signals.topic: No native cryptographic audit trail for multi-agent action provenance
signals.summary: AutoGen lacks native support for cryptographic action receipts (Ed25519-signed, hash-chained) to prove agent actions to external auditors or compliance systems. Enterprise deployments require non-repudiable proof of what each agent executed.
signals.review_reason: Identifies a real enterprise compliance gap: current logging provides traces but lacks cryptographic non-repudiation for audit. signals.topic: Tracing truncation logic causes RecursionError when LLM response contains None values
signals.summary: In `BackendSpanExporter`, when an LLM response contains `None` values and needs truncation, the `_truncated_preview()` method returns a dict containing a boolean `truncated: True`. The `_truncate_mapping_for_json_limit()` function then treats this preview dict as a normal mapping and recursively processes it, causing `_truncated_preview(True)` to return another dict, which is again processed recursively. This results in a `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded`. The bug occurs during trace sanitization/truncation and hides or corrupts the original run error, making debugging impossible.
aliases: trace export stack overflow on None content
tracing crash when truncating NoneType values

The crash hides the original runtime error, making it a significant diagnostic gap. Root cause is clearly identified in the SDK's truncation logic. While count=1, the impact is clear: tracing data (critical for debugging production issues) becomes inaccessible when None values are present.

signals.summary: When using --no-wait to submit a fire-and-forget prompt, the job is queued and returns '[queued] <job-id>' but the queue owner never processes it, silently losing the prompt. No error is returned. The queue owner process is alive but idle. Using --timeout instead of --no-wait is a workaround but changes blocking behavior.
signals.review_reason: User-submitted prompts via --no-wait are silently lost — the command returns a queue confirmation but the work is never executed. The queue owner process is alive and responsive to normal prompts, but entries submitted via --no-wait are ignored. This causes silent data loss: the user gets no error, no result, and no indication the prompt was dropped. This is a functional failure of a documented ACP feature, not a degraded experience.

source_issues.title: [BUG] --no-wait queues prompt but queue owner never processes it
source_issues.evidence: acpx --approve-all codex --no-wait returns [queued] immediately but file is never created. acpx codex status shows session as 'running' with pid but no work done. Regular prompts (without --no-wait) work fine, confirming queue owner is alive but ignores --no-wait queue entries. Only workaround: use --timeout instead (changes blocking semantics). Prompt is silently lost with no error.

signals.topic: WSL→Windows agent cross-environment: cwd path format incompatibility causes session/new to fail
signals.summary: When ACPX embedded runtime runs on WSL and spawns a Windows .exe agent (e.g., copilot.exe), the cwd passed to session/new is a Linux path that Windows agents cannot resolve, causing InternalError -32603. Windows UNC paths and native Windows paths work; Linux paths and /mnt/c/ paths do not.
signals.review_reason: Cross-environment agent spawning is a core use case that is completely broken: WSL hosts cannot spawn Windows .exe agents because the Linux cwd path is passed to the Windows process which cannot resolve it. The session/new request fails with a structured error. This blocks any WSL user trying to use Windows-native agents (copilot.exe, etc.) through ACPX. The fix path is clear but the workaround (manual wslpath -w) is non-obvious.

source_issues.title: WSL→Windows cwd path translation when spawning Windows .exe agents from WSL
source_issues.evidence: When spawning Windows .exe agents from WSL, session/new receives cwd=/home/user/.openclaw/workspace and agent returns error -32603 'Directory does not exist or cannot be accessed'. WSL detection via /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop and .exe suffix detection can identify this case. wslpath -w converts correctly to C:\ or \\wsl.localhost\ paths.

signals.topic: CLI --session flag silently ignored in exec mode, confusing AI agents and wasting credits
signals.summary: The --session flag on the top-level acpx command is silently ignored when exec mode is used, making it look like session mode is active when it is not. AI agents trying to use sessions via acpx claude --session xxx are actually running in exec/one-shot mode with no session, causing 'No acpx session found' errors. Users report burning wrong command 3 times, wasting API credits each time.
aliases: exec mode session flag silent fail
signals.review_reason: The --session flag silently does nothing in exec mode instead of either using the session or throwing a clear error. This causes repeated failed attempts (documented as 3 times), wasting API credits each time. While it is a UX/design issue rather than a crash, the documented financial impact (wasted API credits) and the fact that AI agents must use this CLI every session elevates it to a real user pain point. The fix (warn or error) is straightforward.

source_issues.title: CLI command structure is extremely confusing for AI agents — acpx claude vs acpx claude prompt vs acpx claude exec
source_issues.evidence: acpx claude --session e4f29a00 returns 'No acpx session found' 3 times in a row because --session is silently ignored in exec mode. The correct form is acpx claude prompt --session. Each failed attempt wastes user time and API credits. Author is an AI agent that has to use these commands every session.

signals.topic: Parser mishandles escaped characters in quoted args, corrupting --args-json payloads
signals.summary: The tokenization logic in parsePipeline/tokenizeCommand incorrectly processes escape sequences inside quoted arguments. This causes two distinct failure modes: (1) backslashes inside double-quoted args alter JSON escape content, changing payload semantics; (2) escaped apostrophes inside single-quoted args are treated as quote terminators, causing parse failures with Unclosed quote errors. Pipelines passing prompt-rich JSON through --args-json — especially payloads with apostrophes or multi-line content — break silently or throw parse errors.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional bug causing parse failures in the core tokenization layer. When --args-json payloads contain apostrophes or escape sequences — common in LLM prompt content — the parser either throws 'Unclosed quote' errors or silently corrupts JSON semantics. This is a real execution failure (not a hypothetical feature request), with two concrete reproduction cases. Count=1 single-repo P1 is appropriate since it represents a real bug in a core data-passing mechanism, not a speculative improvement.

source_issues.title: Parser mishandles escaped characters in quoted args, breaking --args-json payloads
source_issues.evidence: Two documented failure modes: (A) escaped apostrophe in single-quoted JSON causes 'Unclosed quote' parse errors; (B) escaped newlines/backslashes in double-quoted JSON alter payload semantics. Explicitly described as breaking existing pipelines that pass prompt-rich JSON through --args-json.

signals.topic: Approval gate resume tokens exceed chat-platform button payload limits, breaking one-tap approval on Telegram and Discord
signals.summary: Lobster generates base64-encoded JWT-style resume tokens (~150+ chars) for approval gates. Telegram's inline button payload limit is 64 bytes and Discord's is 100 chars — both too short. This breaks the core human-in-the-loop approval mechanism on the two most popular chat surfaces. Users are forced to copy-paste long tokens from text messages. The team has acknowledged a two-step workaround hack (hardcoded /restart callback routed to lobster resume backend) but notes it is 'brittle and workflow-specific'.
aliases: resume token length exceeds platform limits
signals.review_reason: This is a real UX blocking issue for the core human-in-the-loop mechanism. Approval gates — a key Lobster feature — cannot be presented as one-tap buttons on Telegram and Discord, the two dominant chat platforms. The team has already built a brittle workaround indicating active user impact. Users must manually copy-paste ~150 char tokens, which is a clear experience degradation for a critical workflow step. Count=1 single-repo P1 is appropriate as this blocks a primary UX flow on widely-used platforms.

source_issues.title: Approval tokens too long for chat-surface buttons (Telegram, Discord)
source_issues.evidence: Platform payload limits explicitly documented: Telegram 64 bytes, Discord 100 chars. Tokens ~150+ chars exceed both. Workaround is 'brittle and workflow-specific'. One-tap approval broken on top two chat surfaces. Proposed alternatives (short approval codes, webhook URL, named slots) indicate this is a real UX break in a primary workflow feature.

signals.topic: Windows: `ollama launch openclaw` spawns duplicate gateway when OpenClaw Gateway is already running as a Scheduled Task (Session 0), causing port conflict, RPC failure, and EPERM file errors
signals.summary: On Windows, running `ollama launch openclaw` when the OpenClaw Gateway is already running as a Scheduled Task in Session 0 creates a second node.exe process that also binds to port 18789. Because user-session processes cannot enumerate Session 0 processes, the Ollama launch integration fails to detect the existing gateway and starts a duplicate one.
aliases: duplicate gateway process on Windows Session 0
port 18789 conflict on Windows scheduled task gateway startup
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed Windows-specific bug where the Ollama launch integration fails to detect an existing gateway running in Session 0, causing a duplicate process that creates port conflicts (port 18789 bound twice), RPC probe failures, EPERM file-access errors, and mDNS name conflicts. It directly breaks the 'ollama launch openclaw' workflow and causes cascading errors including gateway instability. Though count=1, the severity is high with explicit root cause analysis and multiple observable failure symptoms.

source_issues.title: [Windows] ollama launch openclaw starts duplicate gateway when Scheduled Task is already running
source_issues.evidence: Reporter confirmed: two LISTENING entries on port 18789 (netstat); Bonjour mDNS name conflict (`DESKTOP-xxx (OpenClaw) (2)`); RPC probe fails; EPERM errors writing to `~/.openclaw/devices/pending.json`; mass handshake timeout and gateway closed (1006) errors. Root cause identified as Windows Session 0 isolation preventing cross-session process enumeration. Repo Assist confirmed with `bug` + `needs investigation` labels.

signals.topic: Windows Tray App (Node Mode) does not auto-reconnect after Gateway restart, leaving node disconnected until manually toggled
signals.summary: When the OpenClaw Gateway restarts, the Windows Tray App (Node Mode) stays in a disconnected state indefinitely and does not automatically reconnect, unlike the CLI node which implements automatic retry logic.
aliases: tray app node disconnected after gateway restart
windows tray node mode no auto-reconnect
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug where the Windows Tray App (Node Mode) fails to reconnect after a gateway restart, leaving the node in a permanently disconnected state without any automatic retry. The CLI node handles this correctly, creating an inconsistent experience. Users must manually toggle Node Mode off/on to recover, which is a non-trivial workaround for a routine gateway restart scenario. This impacts the node's availability and requires manual intervention.

source_issues.title: Windows Tray App does not auto-reconnect after Gateway restart
source_issues.evidence: Reporter confirmed: after gateway restart, tray app shows `[INFO] Node status changed: Disconnected` and remains disconnected indefinitely — no reconnection attempts logged afterward. CLI node (`openclaw node run`) correctly implements reconnect logic (`Node reconnecting in 1000ms (attempt 1)`), but tray app lacks this. Manual workaround: toggle Node Mode off → wait 2-3s → toggle back on. Repo Assist investigated and identified version/TLS/dispose as contributing causes, applied `bug` + `needs investigation` labels.

signals.topic: Gateway restart storm crashes low-resource hosts when gateway.mode config is missing
signals.summary: Missing gateway.mode in config causes the gateway process to exit with code 1 on startup. Since systemd uses Restart=always without StartLimitBurst, the process restarts every 5 seconds indefinitely, consuming all CPU on 1-vCPU/2GiB hosts and making SSH/VNC unresponsive, requiring hard reboot.
signals.review_reason: Full host unavailability requiring hard reboot is a critical P0. Affects all users on low-resource hosts who omit gateway.mode. Restart storm is a well-documented crash loop causing complete host unavailability, not just a software error.

source_issues.title: Gateway enters restart storm when gateway.mode is missing, making low-resource hosts unresponsive
source_issues.evidence: Missing gateway.mode causes gateway process to exit code 1. Systemd Restart=always without StartLimitBurst causes restart every 5s indefinitely. On 1vCPU/2GiB host this consumes all CPU, making SSH and VNC completely unresponsive, requiring hard reboot.

signals.topic: openclaw run command fails when plugins.allow is configured without explicit 'run' entry, breaking existing cron jobs and bash scripts
signals.summary: A recent version changed openclaw run to be a gated plugin. Users with existing plugins.allow configs that don't include 'run' now get silent failures on their cron jobs and bash scripts, with no deprecation warning.
signals.review_reason: Breaking existing automation pipelines (cron jobs, bash scripts) without deprecation warning is a significant workflow disruption. While count=1, the impact on automated workflows and the silent failure mode warrant P1.

source_issues.title: openclaw run fails when plugins.allow is configured without 'run' entry
source_issues.evidence: openclaw run CLI command fails when plugins.allow is configured without 'run' entry. Breaks existing cron jobs and bash scripts after upgrading to version where 'run' became a gated plugin. Affects automated pipelines relying on openclaw run.

signals.review_reason: Agents stopping mid-task without any output or error is a significant user experience regression. It blocks the main workflow by requiring manual re-activation. Marked as regression by the reporter, confirming it worked before.

signals.review_reason: Cron jobs are automated workflows, and 100% failure rate for OpenAI-based cron runs due to an unhandled thinking parameter is a clear workflow-blocking issue. The reporter references two prior related issues showing this is a recurring pattern, not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: Cron agentTurn sends thinking=none to OpenAI (gpt-5-nano 400) even when thinking=minimal

Confusing retry loop on network failure
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation: the error message falsely attributes a local network problem to API provider outages, causing user confusion and wasting time with unnecessary retries. User specifically notes that the claude CLI works fine, proving the API is reachable — the real issue is network access to raw.githubusercontent.com (litellm dependency). This misdiagnosis is a meaningful experience degradation even though it's a single report.

source_issues.title: Network unreachable? Not here. Mystery
source_issues.evidence: User with network restrictions gets 'litellm.InternalServerError: AnthropicException - [Errno 101] Network is unreachable. The API provider's servers are down or overloaded' message and sees continuous retry loop. Same error occurs with claude CLI (which works) and gemini model. The error message is actively misleading — network is the issue, not the API provider.

aliases: TypeScript provider transitive imports fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
promptfoo transpiles provider .ts but not its dependencies

source_issues.title: TypeScript provider fails when importing other .ts files from the project

remote generation mandate prevents local MCP scanning

source_issues.title: Unable to run MCP scan - Remote generation mandated

aliases: Redteam grader plugins missing prompts cause invariant crash
harmful plugins error on missing prompt configuration
