signals.summary: Vertex AI 上的 Claude Sonnet 模型不支持 systemInstruction 配置参数（而 Gemini 模型支持），导致用户无法通过配置注入系统指令，需手动在 prompt 中拼接 {role: system} 结构，违反了跨模型配置一致性的期望。
aliases: Claude models on Vertex AI do not respect systemInstruction
system prompt not working for vertex claude-sonnet-4-6
signals.review_reason: Vertex AI Claude 模型忽略 systemInstruction 参数导致 prompt 配置不一致，需手动 workaround，但该问题有明确复现步骤，真实影响用户评测配置，属于功能缺陷，count=1 降为 P2。

source_issues.title: Vertex claude model is not using systemInstruction
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 vertex:claude-sonnet-4-6 配置 systemInstruction 时参数被忽略（Gemini 模型正常），尝试 system 参数名也无效，需用 JSON.stringify 手动拼接 system role workaround

signals.topic: ElasticsearchStore sync methods break in ASGI environments (run_until_complete event loop conflict)
signals.summary: ElasticsearchStore wraps all sync methods via asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(), which causes RuntimeError in ASGI deployments (Gunicorn/Uvicorn) when clients are pooled across requests, plus breaks close() in sync contexts.
signals.review_reason: Count=2 (same bug reported twice independently), affects production ASGI deployments. Complete mainflow failure: sync query() and close() methods crash at runtime with RuntimeError. Requires users to write their own replacement store as workaround.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore sync methods use run_until_complete — breaks in ASGI with pooled clients
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Task got Future attached to a different loop. ASGI deployments with pooled AsyncElasticsearch clients crash on query() and close() with full stack trace.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore sync methods use run_until_complete — breaks in ASGI with pooled clients
source_issues.evidence: Same issue reported independently: RuntimeError on close() in ASGI sync thread context. Affects production Gunicorn+Uvicorn deployments with connection pooling.

signals.topic: IngestionPipeline with num_workers>1 silently drops all cache writes, causing re-execution of expensive embedding operations
signals.summary: Multi-worker IngestionPipeline passes a cache copy to worker processes; cache writes in workers are never merged back into the parent, so subsequent runs re-execute transformations (including embedding) that were expected to be cached.
aliases: IngestionPipeline cache not merged from workers
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss in main data ingestion path: multi-worker cache writes are silently discarded, causing expensive embedding operations to be re-executed on every pipeline run. Clear cost impact for users with large document sets. No crash but significant performance/cost regression.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: IngestionPipeline with `num_workers > 1` silently loses all cache writes
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code shows sequential cache after first run=1, after second run=1 (correct). Multi-worker cache after first run=0, after second run=0 (all writes silently lost). Each worker mutates its own in-memory copy which is discarded on exit.

signals.topic: Bedrock converse streaming retry decorator is silently inert on async generators — throttling/errors never trigger retries
signals.summary: The @retry_decorator on _conversion_stream_with_retry (async generator) never fires because tenacity cannot intercept exceptions during async generator iteration — only the initial call. Retryable errors (ThrottlingException, ServiceUnavailableException) are silently swallowed.
signals.review_reason: Silent failure in AWS Bedrock streaming path: retry logic is completely inert, so throttling and service errors cause streaming failures with no retry. Clear reliability impact for production AWS Bedrock users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: @retry_decorator on async generator _conversion_stream_with_retry is silently inert
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code demonstrates tenacity @retry on an async generator never retries: gen_with_retry called only once even when ValueError is raised mid-stream. Comment in code acknowledges 'This is a bit of a hack'. No retry ever fires for streaming calls.

signals.topic: Refine synthesizer crashes with uncaught ValueError/TypeError from structured output (function-calling path)
signals.summary: When using output_cls with function-calling LLMs, Refine only catches ValidationError but not ValueError/TypeError raised by failed/missing tool calls in structured_predict, causing query to crash instead of falling back to warning path.
aliases: structured_predict error not caught in Refine
signals.review_reason: Main query path crash: when structured output (output_cls) is used with function-calling models and the LLM fails to produce tool calls, the entire query crashes instead of gracefully falling back. Full stack trace provided. This is a regression from v0.14.18.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Refine does not catch `ValueError`/`TypeError` from tool-calling structured outputs
source_issues.evidence: Full traceback shows ValueError propagates through structured_predict -> FunctionCallingProgram -> Refine._give_response_single -> query engine, crashing the entire query. Was working before v0.14.18.

signals.topic: DocumentSummaryIndex.delete_nodes() crashes with KeyError on invalid node IDs instead of skipping them
signals.summary: delete_nodes() mutates its input list while iterating, causing some invalid IDs to remain. Those IDs are then passed to _index_struct.delete_nodes() which raises KeyError on dict lookup.
aliases: invalid node ID crash in delete_nodes
signals.review_reason: delete_nodes() crashes on predictable user scenario (deleting a mix of valid and invalid node IDs). Clear exception with stack trace. Low count but the crash is in a main index management method.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `DocumentSummaryIndex.delete_nodes()` crashes on invalid node IDs instead of skipping them
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with 2 invalid IDs: KeyError: 'does_not_exist_2'. Full traceback through document_summary.py:67 showing dict lookup failure on invalid node ID.

signals.topic: ESM/CJS regression: autopilot and claims commands crash with 'require is not defined' on fresh install
signals.summary: Three compiled ESM files in @claude-flow/cli contain bare `require()` calls (crypto, fs, path) without `createRequire` shim, causing all autopilot and claims subcommands to fail immediately with 'require is not defined' on any v3.5.75 install. Blocks headline v3 features on fresh install and new machine setup.
signals.review_reason: count=4 confirmed distinct reports; main flow blocking (autopilot+claims fail on fresh install); reproducible by any new user; all 4 agree on same root cause (bare require in ESM); workaround requires re-patching on every upgrade — clear user burden.

source_issues.title: Bug: bare require() calls in ESM modules cause 'require is not defined' on autopilot/claims commands (v3.5.75)
source_issues.evidence: Clean install crashes on first use of headline v3 features. Severity High. Workaround requires sed patching node_modules on every upgrade.

source_issues.title: [Bug] ruflo autopilot and ruflo claims fail on fresh 3.5.75 install — bare require() calls inside ESM modules
source_issues.evidence: Blocks autopilot and claims on fresh install. Affects new users and new machine setup. Workaround must be reapplied on every npm install -g.

source_issues.title: Bug: autopilot commands fail with 'require is not defined' (CJS in ESM package)
source_issues.evidence: All autopilot subcommands (status, enable, disable, config, reset, log, learn, history, predict, check) fail immediately.

source_issues.title: ESM/CJS regression in 3.5.75
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression in v3.5.75. Users need workaround via session-start hook patching node_modules.

signals.topic: CLI one-shot and memory commands hang indefinitely after completing — process.exit() missing
signals.summary: ruflo memory store/retrieve/search and other one-shot CLI commands complete their operation successfully but never exit, requiring manual kill. ControllerRegistry keeps Node.js event loop alive. Breaks automation scripts, programmatic consumers, and MCP paths.
signals.review_reason: 2 distinct reports confirming same root cause; operation succeeds but never exits, breaking automation, scripts, and MCP; workaround via background+sleep+kill is painful and not viable for MCP path; the self-learning loop core feature is broken.

source_issues.title: CLI one-shot commands (memory store, memory retrieve) hang indefinitely after completing
source_issues.evidence: Operation completes in 3-5ms with correct output but process never exits. Root cause: ControllerRegistry opens DB connections + timers that keep event loop alive. Breaks automation scripts that shell out to ruflo and expect process exit. Accumulates zombie Node.js processes on repeated calls.

source_issues.title: Memory subcommands still hang on v3.5.75 — original fix in #1453 appears incomplete
source_issues.evidence: Regression from fixed issue #1453. Confirmed on latest v3.5.75. Semantically correct results returned but process hangs. Breaks the self-learning loop (LEARN → COORD → EXECUTE → REMEMBER) for programmatic consumers.

signals.topic: plugin-code-intelligence: all 5 MCP tools return empty results due to stub helper functions
signals.summary: The plugin-code-intelligence plugin's 3 core helper functions (getFilesInPath, performSemanticSearch, getAllRelatedFiles) are stub implementations returning empty data. GNNBridge.extractImports() also returns []. All 5 MCP tools (code/semantic-search, code/architecture-analyze, code/refactor-impact, code/split-suggest, code/learn-patterns) return structurally correct but empty results. Package references non-existent WASM modules.
signals.review_reason: count=2 distinct reports from same author covering same issue; all 5 MCP tools are non-functional (marketed capabilities return empty); architecture analysis produces meaningless graphs (0 edges); no workaround; real WASM packages referenced by wrong names.

source_issues.title: plugin-code-intelligence: stub implementations prevent all 5 MCP tools from returning real results
source_issues.evidence: 3 stub functions return []/empty, GNNBridge.extractImports returns []. All 5 tools return structurally correct but empty results. Package references non-existent ruvector-gnn-wasm/ruvector-mincut-wasm. Real WASM packages have different APIs.

source_issues.title: plugin-code-intelligence: stub implementations prevent MCP tools from returning real results
source_issues.evidence: Semantic search always returns 0 results. Architecture analysis produces nodes but 0 edges (no dependency relationships). Refactor impact only sees directly changed files. WASM modules throw 'not implemented'. Plugin is non-functional.

signals.topic: Memory commands ignore CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD — bare process.cwd() breaks MCP memory tools under Claude Desktop
signals.summary: ruflo memory list/store/retrieve/retrieve commands do not honor the CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD environment variable introduced in v3.5.52, falling back to bare process.cwd(). Claude Desktop launches MCP server from non-workspace cwd, making memory tools return 'Database not found' or 'Database not initialized' even when the real DB is populated.
aliases: memory tools broken in Claude Desktop
memory db not found Claude Desktop
signals.review_reason: Main integration path (Claude Desktop MCP) is blocked for memory tools specifically; PR #1534 fixed other tools but memory path was missed; causes silent data-loss appearance (0 entries when DB is populated); workaround requires wrapper cd before exec, which defeats PR #1534's stated goal.

source_issues.title: [Bug] memory commands ignore CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD — bare process.cwd() in memory-bridge.js and memory-initializer.js breaks MCP memory tools under Claude Desktop
source_issues.evidence: Claude Desktop integration for memory tools is completely broken. mcp__ruflo__memory_list returns empty, memory_store errors with 'Database not initialized'. 16+ bare process.cwd() call sites identified in memory-bridge.js and memory-initializer.js. Every other MCP tool was fixed by PR #1534; memory path was missed.

signals.topic: MCP tools use process.cwd() resolving to System32 on Windows — all state-persistence tools fail
signals.summary: All MCP tool files in mcp-tools/ use process.cwd() to build storage paths. On Windows, AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) launch MCP servers via npx from System32, causing EPERM on every storage-path operation. All 16+ MCP tool files are affected, making the entire MCP tool suite non-functional on Windows.
signals.review_reason: All 16+ MCP tool files affected on Windows; entire MCP suite is non-functional for Windows AI agent users; EPERM is a clear, reproducible failure; workaround requires manual env var setup per launch.

source_issues.title: MCP tools use process.cwd() which resolves to System32 on Windows
source_issues.evidence: All 16+ MCP tool files (swarm, agent, session, github, hive-mind, neural, etc.) fail with EPERM when run from Windows AI agents. Most AI coding agents do not set cwd when launching MCP servers. Entire MCP tool suite is non-functional for Windows users.

signals.topic: Page navigates to about:blank after form submission or navigation (CDP target loss)
signals.summary: CDP target is lost after form submission or SPA navigation, causing the tab to switch to about:blank. All subsequent commands operate on a dead page. Blocks authentication workflows.
signals.review_reason: Multiple confirmed regression paths all leading to about:blank: (1) form submission SPA navigation loses CDP target on every tested framework (#1157), (2) open command regression in headless CI since v0.24.1 with 100% failure rate across 50+ runs (#1177), (3) PR_SET_PDEATHSIG regression killing Chrome after 7s idle (#1148). All are high-frequency, main-flow blocking, and reproducible. Combined they represent the most severe ongoing reliability issue.

source_issues.title: CDP target lost after form submission / SPA navigation — tab becomes about:blank
source_issues.evidence: After submitting a login form, the active CDP target switches to about:blank. tab list shows [0] about:blank. snapshot returns (empty page). This makes agent-browser unusable for any workflow that requires authentication via form submission.

source_issues.title: open command navigates to about:blank since 0.24.1 (headless CI)
source_issues.evidence: Since v0.24.1, open command leaves browser on about:blank instead of navigating to target URL. 100% failure rate on >=0.24.1 across 50+ CI runs. Screenshot shows blank white page. Blocks automated browser testing of preview deployments.

source_issues.title: fix: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills Chrome in tokio multi-threaded runtime (v0.24.1 regression)
source_issues.evidence: v0.24.1 introduced PR_SET_PDEATHSIG which causes Chrome to be killed after ~7-9 seconds idle on every page. get url returns about:blank. All downloads broken (first works, second fails). Any automation taking >7s between commands fails. 100% reproducible.

signals.topic: Existing Chrome / remote CDP attachment fails — hangs, blocked sockets, or missing page-level support
signals.summary: Attaching agent-browser to existing Chrome instances or remote CDP endpoints fails in multiple scenarios: hangs indefinitely on macOS, blocked by sandbox syscalls in Claude Code, and lacks page-level WebSocket support.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct but related failure modes for the core use case of attaching to existing/remote Chrome: (1) hangs indefinitely on macOS with externally-launched Chrome via HTTP discovery (#1193), (2) completely blocked in Claude Code sandbox due to Unix socket syscall restrictions (#1155), (3) no page-level WebSocket support blocking embedding frameworks (#1185). Combined count=3, all block auth-state reuse and external Chrome integration workflows — a primary advertised use case.

source_issues.title: --cdp attach to existing Chrome instance hangs indefinitely on macOS (Chrome 139)
source_issues.evidence: agent-browser tab list --cdp 9222 hangs indefinitely when connecting to an already-running Chrome instance. Cannot use agent-browser with externally-managed Chrome instances (other AI tools' browser sessions, user's existing browser with auth state). Forces users to let agent-browser launch its own Chrome with no auth state reuse.

source_issues.title: CLI unusable in Claude Code sandbox: Unix domain socket bind/connect blocked
source_issues.evidence: All agent-browser CLI commands fail in Claude Code sandbox because daemon requires Unix domain socket IPC blocked by sandbox syscall restrictions. Daemon error: Failed to bind socket: Operation not permitted. Makes agent-browser completely unusable in Claude Code environments.

source_issues.title: feat(cli): add --direct flag to connect for page-level CDP WebSocket URLs
source_issues.evidence: agent-browser connect assumes browser-level CDP endpoints and always uses Target.* commands. Fails on page-level WebSocket URLs (ws://localhost:19222/devtools/page/ABC123) because page sessions do not support browser-level calls. Blocks integrations with embedding frameworks that expose per-tab isolation through page-level WebSocket URLs.

signals.topic: Session state (cookies, localStorage, HTTPS settings) not persisted or inherited across restarts and contexts
signals.summary: Cookies and localStorage are not restored from saved state files on Linux. Session-scoped CDP settings (user-agent, color-scheme, HTTPS ignore) are not applied to recording contexts.
aliases: HTTPS ignore not applied in recording
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed failures of session state propagation: (1) cookies/localStorage saved to state file are silently not restored on Linux (#1164), directly breaking the advertised persistent-auth workflow, (2) HTTPS ignore settings not applied to recording context blocks self-signed cert workflows (#1172). Both are silent failures (no error message) that cause timeouts and broken authentication.

source_issues.title: Linux v0.24.1: state save/--state and --session-name write state but do not restore cookies or localStorage
source_issues.evidence: state save writes a JSON file containing expected cookie and localStorage entry, but the next launch with --state still restores neither. Same for --session-name auto persistence. This blocks the main documented workflow: save auth/session once, reuse across later runs.

source_issues.title: Recording context does not inherit --ignore-https-errors / AGENT_BROWSER_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS
source_issues.evidence: When AGENT_BROWSER_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS=true, main browser ignores cert errors but recording context created by record start does NOT inherit this setting. goto after record start fails with Operation timed out on self-signed HTTPS pages. Blocks headless visual verification of local dev apps using self-signed certs.

signals.topic: Snapshot accessibility tree truncated over remote CDP WebSocket (regression)
signals.summary: snapshot --json returns severely truncated accessibility tree (~715 chars vs ~3000-5000 chars) when connecting via remote CDP WebSocket, causing automated element filtering to return zero results.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression where remote CDP WebSocket users get an accessibility tree missing all popover/dynamic content. Any workflow using snapshot refs to identify interactive elements (radio buttons, tabs, etc.) breaks silently — filtering returns zero results without error. Local connections unaffected, making this a remote-specific regression likely in the WebSocket serialization path.

source_issues.title: snapshot --json returns truncated accessibility tree over remote CDP WebSocket
source_issues.evidence: Over remote CDP WebSocket, snapshot -i -c --json returns ~715 chars (only page-level elements) instead of ~3000-5000 chars including all interactive elements inside popovers. Filtering data.refs for role==radio returns 0 results. Regression from v0.19.0 where this worked correctly. Local browser works fine with same code.

signals.topic: Headed mode: viewport config ignored and screenshots are completely black when using fullscreen or maximized
signals.summary: When using --start-fullscreen or --start-maximized in headed mode, viewport config is ignored and screenshots produce completely black images, blocking visual verification workflows.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed headed-mode visual verification failure: screenshots are completely black (not just wrong size), and viewport is silently ignored when fullscreen. Blocks automated visual regression testing workflows that rely on headed mode + fullscreen. Workaround (macOS screencapture) is platform-specific and loses the structured screenshot API.

source_issues.title: Headed mode: viewport config ignored and screenshots black when using --start-fullscreen or --start-maximized
source_issues.evidence: With --start-fullscreen in headed mode, agent-browser screenshot produces a completely black image. window.innerWidth/Height reports 800x623 instead of configured 1728x1117. No workaround that preserves both fullscreen and working screenshots. Users must fall back to macOS native screencapture.

signals.topic: Anthropic adapter orphaned tool_use causes API rejection and permanently bricks session state
signals.summary: When a tool call enters output-error state, the Anthropic adapter drops the matching tool_result during internal conversion, producing API payloads with orphaned tool_use blocks. Anthropic API responds with 400 rejection. The broken session state persists across turns because every subsequent message rebuilds the same broken payload, permanently blocking the agent flow.
aliases: session permanently broken after tool error
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure — API call rejection permanently bricks the agent session. The tool call + error result are stored correctly at the Model layer but get corrupted during Anthropic-specific adapter conversion, making recovery impossible without manual session reset.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/anthropic: adapter produces orphaned tool_use without matching tool_result for output-error state tools
source_issues.evidence: API rejects with 400: messages.N: tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks. Session permanently stuck because every turn rebuilds the same broken payload from the error history.

signals.topic: AI Gateway error conversion strips APICallError marker, silently disabling SDK maxRetries
signals.summary: The AI Gateway converts retryable APICallError instances (503, 429, 408) into GatewayInternalServerError before they reach the SDK retry logic. Since the retry function checks APICallError.isInstance(error), Gateway errors lack the required marker and maxRetries is never activated.
aliases: transient errors not retried through Gateway
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation — retry setting is silently ignored for all Gateway-proxied requests. Transient provider errors that should succeed on retry instead cause complete request failures.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway breaks SDK retry: GatewayInternalServerError not recognized by maxRetries
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction confirms GatewayInternalServerError lacks vercel.ai.error.AI_APICallError symbol marker, so isRetryable is undefined and maxRetries never triggers for 503/429/408 errors.

signals.topic: AI Gateway mid-conversation failover to Vertex fails with thought signature incompatibility
signals.summary: When using Gateway with multi-provider failover order (google then vertex), a transient 503 from Google AI Studio triggers automatic failover to Vertex, but Vertex rejects the failover request with 400 'Thought signature is not valid' because thought signatures from Google AI Studio are structurally incompatible with Vertex.
aliases: Vertex rejects Google AI Studio thought tokens on failover
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure — the automatic failover feature actively breaks the session when triggered. Users relying on failover for resilience experience complete request failures instead of seamless recovery.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: Vertex rejects thought signatures from Google AI Studio on mid-conversation failover
source_issues.evidence: Multi-step agent session using google/gemini-3-flash with order: ['google', 'vertex']. After 10+ tool call steps, Google returns 503 and Gateway fails over to Vertex, which immediately rejects with 400 'Thought signature is not valid'.

signals.topic: AI Gateway returns 503 on Gemini 3 Flash with no automatic retry or fallback
signals.summary: Gateway returns 503 Service Temporarily Unavailable for google/gemini-3-flash during preview model capacity issues. The response indicates isRetryable:true and fallbacksAvailable:[] but Gateway makes no retry and no fallback, causing complete request failure.
aliases: preview model outage causes complete failure
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure — users experience complete outages during transient provider capacity issues. The Gateway acknowledges errors as retryable but does not act on it, wasting the retry opportunity.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: Google Gemini 3 Flash returns 503 with no automatic fallback
source_issues.evidence: Gateway returns 503 with isRetryable:true in metadata. Only 1 attempt is made. Fallback models exist but Gateway does not trigger them automatically for this error.

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock explicit credentials incorrectly merged with AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from environment causing auth failures
signals.summary: When users pass explicit accessKeyId/secretAccessKey to createAmazonBedrock, the SDK still attaches AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from the environment via loadOptionalSetting fallback. On EKS IRSA, ECS task roles, and Lambda (where AWS_SESSION_TOKEN is always set for workload identity), the merged credentials are invalid and AWS returns 'The security token included in the request is invalid'.
aliases: AWS credentials merged with env session token
Lambda IAM role credential override broken
Amazon Bedrock auth invalid security token
signals.review_reason: Authentication failures in cloud production environments — explicit credentials are a documented usage pattern that is completely broken on major AWS compute services. Users cannot use IAM user credentials in EKS/Lambda contexts.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: explicit accessKeyId/secretAccessKey should not merge AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from env
source_issues.evidence: loadOptionalSetting falls back to process.env.AWS_SESSION_TOKEN even when explicit credentials are provided. On EKS/ECS/Lambda where AWS_SESSION_TOKEN is set for workload identity, the merged credentials produce 'security token is invalid' errors.

signals.topic: `export type` in "use server" files incorrectly registered as Server Action causing build failures and runtime ReferenceError
signals.summary: In Next.js 16.1.x, `export type` declarations in "use server" files are incorrectly treated as Server Actions by the SWC post-pass (server_actions.rs). This causes `registerServerReference()` calls for TypeScript-only identifiers that don't exist at runtime, leading to build errors in Turbopack monorepos and `ReferenceError: Foo is not defined` at runtime. Regression from PR #86296.
aliases: export type use server Server Action incorrect registration
export type in use server causes ReferenceError
signals.review_reason: Two issues confirming a regression where `export type` in "use server" files breaks both builds (in monorepos) and runtime execution. This affects any project using Server Actions with TypeScript type re-exports — a common pattern. Both build-time and runtime failures make this P0.

source_issues.title: `export type` in "use server" file incorrectly registered as Server Action (v16.1.x regression)
source_issues.evidence: Turbopack generates an `actions.js` aggregation file that re-exports all registered Server Actions. Types incorrectly registered cause `Export TranscriptState doesn't exist in target module` build errors in larger monorepos.

source_issues.title: `export type` in "use server" file causes runtime ReferenceError in v16.1.x (regression from PR #86296)
source_issues.evidence: Runtime `ReferenceError: Foo is not defined` in production because TypeScript erases the type at compile time but `registerServerReference()` still references it. Regression from v16.0.3 behavior.

signals.topic: Testing API `unstable_getResponseFromNextConfig` silently fails with async function configs in next.config
signals.summary: The testing API `unstable_getResponseFromNextConfig` does not resolve async function configs (the `(phase, ctx) => Promise<NextConfig>` pattern commonly used by plugins like `withSentry`, `withWorkflow`, etc.). Config properties like rewrites/redirects return `null` silently, causing test assertions to pass incorrectly.
aliases: testing server API async function next config
signals.review_reason: Testing API silently produces false-negative results for async-config setups. This is a lesser-impact issue (affects test authors, not end users) and does not block main flows. P2 appropriate.

source_issues.title: unstable_getResponseFromNextConfig does not resolve async function configs
source_issues.evidence: Async function configs (e.g. `(phase, ctx) => config` pattern) are passed directly to `loadCustomRoutes` without resolution, causing all rewrite/redirect/header matches to return `null` silently in tests. Popular plugins like withSentry and withWorkflow use this pattern.

source_issues.title: unstable_getResponseFromNextConfig does not support async function configs
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #92500. The testing API silently produces incorrect test results for any next.config using async function pattern, which is the standard plugin pattern.

signals.topic: Vulnerable lodash@4.17.23 (CVE-2026-4800) bundled in Next.js dist/compiled — blocks security scanning and upgrades
signals.summary: Next.js 16.2.2 ships lodash@4.17.23 (containing CVE-2026-4800) in pre-compiled `dist/compiled/` files. Security scanners (OWASP Dependency-Check) flag the bundled code and block CI/CD pipelines, preventing teams from upgrading to Next.js 16. The vulnerable code cannot be resolved via npm audit or dependency overlays since it is pre-compiled.
signals.review_reason: While a single CVE report could be excluded, the user impact is concrete: OWASP scanner failures block CI/CD pipelines and prevent teams from upgrading to Next.js 16. The bundled nature of lodash in dist/compiled means no standard mitigation is possible. P1 despite count=2 single-repo due to CI/CD blockage severity.

source_issues.title: Vulnerable lodash@4.17.23 bundled in dist/compiled (CVE-2026-4800)
source_issues.evidence: OWASP Dependency-Check flags GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc in Next.js 16.2.2 bundled lodash. Downstream CI/CD pipelines are blocked. Cannot be resolved via npm audit or overlays because code is in pre-compiled dist/. Users cannot upgrade to Next.js 16 without security scanner failures.

source_issues.title: Vulnerable lodash@4.17.23 bundled in dist/compiled (CVE-2026-4800)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #92454, closed as invalid. Same CVE, same user impact evidence: security scanners flag the bundled code and block deployments.

signals.topic: Turbopack production build passes wrong environment to SWC plugins, breaking production optimization
signals.summary: When using `next build` with Turbopack (default in Next.js 16), SWC plugins receive 'development' instead of 'production' via TransformPluginMetadataContextKind::Env. This breaks minification, tree-shaking, and any environment-sensitive transformations in production builds.
aliases: Turbopack SWC plugin env production build
Turbopack passes development to SWC plugins during next build
signals.review_reason: Production build optimization is a core workflow. Wrong env to SWC plugins means production builds are functionally incorrect — minification and tree-shaking are broken. This is a P0 main-flow blocker.

source_issues.title: Turbopack passes "development" to SWC plugins during next build
source_issues.evidence: Users running `next build --turbopack` get 'development' env instead of 'production', breaking SWC plugin transformations. Has minimal reproduction repo. Webpack build (`--webpack`) correctly outputs 'production'.

signals.topic: Draft Mode: searchParams empty on statically generated pages deployed to Vercel (Next.js 16 regression)
signals.summary: In Next.js 16 App Router deployed to Vercel, when Draft Mode is enabled and a route handler redirects with search parameters, those searchParams are empty on statically generated pages. The same code works correctly on Next.js 15 and locally with `next dev`/`next start`.
aliases: searchParams empty static page draft mode Vercel
signals.review_reason: A documented regression from Next.js 15 to 16 that blocks the official CMS preview integration pattern. Users following the official Next.js Draft Mode documentation cannot pass searchParams on Vercel, which is a primary deployment target.

source_issues.title: [Next.js 16] [App Router] searchParams empty on statically generated pages when Draft Mode is enabled (Vercel only)
source_issues.evidence: Draft Mode with search parameter passthrough broken on Vercel in Next.js 16. Follows official Next.js docs pattern. Blocks CMS preview integration workflows. Vercel-only regression.

signals.topic: createProject API breaking change: secret environment variable type silently removed, breaking existing integrations
signals.summary: The createProject method silently removed support for the 'secret' type when creating environment variables, causing existing user code to break with no deprecation warning, no migration path, and no documentation mention of the change.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: a silent breaking API change that blocks the user's main workflow (project creation with secret environment variables), with no migration path or warning. The issue demonstrates clear production impact — existing working code is broken — which meets the criteria for a workflow-runtime blocking issue, warranting P1 priority (P0 requires count>=3, which is not met with a single issue).

source_issues.title: [BREAKING CHANGE|DOC ISSUE]: vercel.projects.createProject no longer support secret vars so it breaks current code
source_issues.evidence: createProject no longer accepts the 'secret' type for environment variable creation, breaking the reporter's production product. No deprecation warning was given. Documentation does not mention the removal or explain the differences between system, secret, encrypted, plain, and sensitive types.

signals.topic: Dirty .gitignore breaks task input hashing, causing cache permanent miss (regression v2.8.18+)
signals.summary: When .gitignore has any uncommitted modification, turbo v2.8.18+ stops respecting its patterns during task input hashing. Gitignored directories like node_modules/ leak into task inputs, producing different hashes on every run and permanently breaking cache. Introduced by PR #12339.
signals.review_reason: P0 because it is a regression from a previously working version (v2.8.17) that breaks the core caching mechanism. Cache is permanently broken while .gitignore is dirty — the primary performance feature of turbo is defeated for all subsequent runs until the change is committed. The impact is high: in large monorepos turbo walks hundreds of thousands of node_modules files on every invocation. User provided complete reproduction and identified the exact PR that introduced the regression.

source_issues.title: Dirty .gitignore causes gitignored files to leak into task input hashes (v2.8.18+)
source_issues.evidence: User provided full reproduction script. v2.8.17 correct (0 leaking), v2.8.18+ breaks (node_modules/.bin/foo leaks into inputs). Cache permanently broken while .gitignore is dirty — every run produces a new hash. In large monorepos, turbo walks hundreds of thousands of files in node_modules/ on every invocation. Modifying .gitignore before committing is a normal workflow.

signals.topic: Turbo >2.8.14 fails to connect to self-hosted remote cache with custom CA certificates
signals.summary: Turbo versions greater than 2.8.14 intermittently fail to connect to self-hosted remote cache servers (e.g. ducktors/turborepo-remote-cache) when custom CA certificates are used. Connection failures are non-deterministic and affect multiple platforms (macOS arm64, Linux amd64).
aliases: custom CA remote cache connection failure
self-hosted remote cache SSL handshake failure
signals.review_reason: P1 because while it blocks remote caching for self-hosted cache users (a significant use case), the failure is intermittent rather than deterministic, and the workaround (downgrade to 2.8.14) exists. It is not a full workflow blocker for all users — only those with custom CA environments. However, it is a clear regression from v2.8.14 with user-impacting evidence: connection failures with error messages and full reproduction provided.

source_issues.title: Turbo > 2.8.14 fails to connect to self-hosted remote cache server with custom CA
source_issues.evidence: User provided a full reproduction repository. The issue is intermittent (high likelihood but not 100%). Affects macOS arm64 and Linux amd64. Error: 'Could not connect to https://my-hostname:3000/'. Likely related to ApiClient refactoring that introduced the fast client. The workaround is to downgrade to v2.8.14.

signals.topic: Turbo build completely fails on Windows when installed via Bun (spawnSync error, turbo.exe blocked by Windows security)
signals.summary: On Windows, running turbo commands (e.g., bun run build, turbo info) after installing via Bun causes a spawnSync error with errno -4094/UNKNOWN code. The turbo.exe binary is blocked by Windows security, preventing any turbo operations.
aliases: Bun on Windows turbo spawnSync UNKNOWN
turbo.exe blocked on Windows with Bun
signals.review_reason: P1 because it completely blocks the main build workflow (turbo run build) on Windows when using Bun as the package manager. This is a primary workflow failure — users cannot run their builds at all. The Windows security blocking of turbo.exe is a significant and specific blocker. Confidence is slightly reduced as it may be specific to certain Windows security configurations, but the impact is unambiguous.

source_issues.title: Bun run build failed on window on fresh turbo repo
source_issues.evidence: User reports Windows security popup blocking turbo.exe: 'PART OF THIS APP HAS BEEN BLOCKED — Some features of Node.js JavaScript Runtime may not work because we can't confirm who published turbo.exe'. The build completely fails with exit code 1. Multiple attempts to reinstall (deleting node_modules, global install) did not resolve the issue. Affects fresh turbo repo installed via bunx create-turbo@latest.

signals.topic: Binary file hash inconsistency across platforms causes remote cache misses
signals.summary: When using remote cache, turbo generates different hashes for identical binary files (e.g., .png, .tgz) on different build environments (different OS/architecture). This causes cache misses even when the files are byte-for-byte identical, breaking remote cache sharing across CI pipelines.
aliases: remote cache misses for binary files
different hash for identical binary files across environments
signals.review_reason: P1 because it breaks cross-environment remote cache sharing, which is a core turbo feature for CI/CD cost savings. When developers and CI builders produce different hashes for identical binary files, cache is never reused across those boundaries, defeating a major value proposition. Confidence is reduced because the bug label is 'needs: reproduction' suggesting it may not have been confirmed, but the description of the symptom is consistent and specific.

source_issues.title: [turborepo] Remote cache misses due to different hashes for binary files on different build environments
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly demonstrates that .js and text files produce identical hashes across environments, but binary files (png, tgz) produce different hashes. This breaks the core remote cache sharing feature across developer machines and CI builders. No reproduction repo provided but the mechanism is clearly described.

signals.topic: Pruning produces different file hashes for CRLF line ending files
signals.summary: After running turbo prune, the file hashes for files with CRLF line endings differ from the pre-prune hashes, causing remote cache misses for identical content.
aliases: CRLF line endings hash mismatch after prune
turbo prune hash busting CRLF files
signals.review_reason: P1 because it directly breaks the prune feature which is commonly used for Docker image builds and CI. Users relying on turbo prune to create lean container images will get incorrect caching behavior. The root cause (CRLF normalization difference before/after prune) is a clear regression in hashing correctness. User provided a complete reproduction repo.

source_issues.title: Pruning results in different hashes for files with CRLF line endings
source_issues.evidence: User provided a full reproduction repo (turborepo-gitattributes) with a test script demonstrating hash mismatch. File hashes for README-dos-dos.md and README-unix-dos.md differ before and after turbo prune. Likely related to .gitattributes line-ending normalization.

signals.topic: Vercel CLI `vercel env add <name> preview` ignores --yes/--force flags, causing interactive prompts in CI/CD environments
signals.summary: The `vercel env add <name> preview` command always prompts interactively for a git branch even when `--yes`, `--force`, and `--non-interactive` flags are provided. This blocks automation in CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions) because the process hangs waiting for interactive input that cannot be satisfied non-interactively. The CLI's own error output suggests a command that still triggers the same prompt, creating a circular failure.
aliases: CLI env add preview interactive prompt fails CI
vercel env add --force ignored in non-interactive mode
preview environment variable CLI automation broken
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: the CLI's --yes/--force flags are silently ignored for the 'preview' target of `vercel env add`, causing an interactive prompt that hangs in CI/CD pipelines. This is a main-flow blocker for automation use cases. The evidence is concrete: the CLI itself suggests a command that still fails, and the workaround requires bypassing the CLI entirely with the REST API. Count=1 (single issue), so P1 is appropriate — it affects a clear automation workflow but is not a high-frequency repeated pattern.

source_issues.title: CLI: `vercel env add <name> preview` always prompts for git branch even with --yes --force
source_issues.evidence: The CLI prompts interactively for git branch even with --yes --force flags. The exact command suggested by the CLI's own hint still triggers the prompt, making it impossible to automate in CI/CD. User must fall back to REST API as workaround.

signals.topic: Git Graph UI overflow: branch names and tags render outside container
signals.summary: Git Graph 中分支名称和标签溢出其容器边界，元素没有正确换行，导致 UI 布局混乱。这是 Git Graph 视图的高频使用功能，UI 溢出问题影响提交历史的可读性。
signals.review_reason: 两条独立 issue 反映同一根因（Git Graph UI 元素溢出容器），影响 Git 提交历史可读性，是中等用户体验下降。由于 count=2，按规则可给 P2。

source_issues.title: Git graph tags overflow
source_issues.evidence: Git Graph 中标签（tags）溢出容器边界，重设提交信息面板大小后问题仍然存在。提供了截图佐证。

source_issues.title: [Cosmetic][Git graph] Branch Name overflows sidebar
source_issues.evidence: Git Graph 侧边栏中分支名称溢出，没有换行。提供了截图佐证。

signals.topic: Database file load failure prevents project persistence
signals.summary: 用户报告 Zed 无法加载数据库文件，导致项目记录无法保存。这是一种数据持久化失败，直接影响用户工作连续性。
signals.review_reason: 单条 issue，但错误信息明确：数据库文件加载失败导致项目无法保存。这是关键数据持久化功能失效，用户工作进度存在丢失风险，应视为高优先级 P1 而非 P0。

source_issues.title: Failed to load the database file
source_issues.evidence: Zed failed to load the data file. Therefore, projects are no longer being saved. Screenshot shows an error dialog about loading the database file.

signals.topic: Disabled LSPs restart and consume resources despite user-disabled preference
signals.summary: 用户禁用了 PHP LSP (devsense)，但 LSP 进程持续在后台重启，占用 2-3GB 内存，且请求超时（120s+）。用户明确禁用了 LSP 但 Zed 不遵守该设置。
signals.review_reason: 单条 issue 但证据充分：用户禁用了 LSP，Zed 不遵守设置导致进程后台持续运行并消耗 2-3GB 内存，同时大量 LSP 请求超时。这直接造成资源浪费和功能不可用（诊断超时），属于主流程阻断性问题。

source_issues.title: Disabled LSPs don't stay disabled
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确在 Zed 设置中禁用了 devsense PHP LSP (phptools)，但 Activity Monitor 显示有 2-3GB 的 devsense.php.ls 进程在运行（用户没有手动启动）。手动停止后几分钟内 PHP LSP 再次启动。日志显示大量 'Request timed out' 和 'Get diagnostics via phpantom_lsp failed' 错误。

signals.topic: Devcontainer PATH environment silently overwritten, breaking gem-installed tools
signals.summary: Zed 的 devcontainer 集成用最小化的 fallback PATH 覆盖了容器镜像原有的完整 PATH，导致 /usr/local/bundle/bin 等目录从 PATH 中消失，使 gem 安装的工具（如 foreman）无法执行。
signals.review_reason: 单条 issue 但影响明确：devcontainer PATH 被完全覆盖导致 gem 安装的工具链不可用，开发者无法运行正常的工作流（如 foreman 启动本地服务）。这是 devcontainer 集成的核心功能回归。

source_issues.title: devcontainer changes the default PATH environment of the image
source_issues.evidence: Zed devcontainer terminal 的 PATH 是 /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin，而原始 ruby:3.4.8 镜像的 PATH 包含 /usr/local/bundle/bin。用户安装 foreman 后执行 'foreman' 报错 'bash: foreman: command not found'。日志明确显示 Zed 覆盖了 PATH 环境变量。

signals.topic: Wayland GNOME 50 interface sluggishness causing 1+ second freezes
signals.summary: 在 GNOME 50 (Wayland) 上使用 Zed 时，界面出现严重卡顿，文件切换或滚动时出现 1.5 秒以上的冻结。只有切换到 XWayland 才能规避问题。疑似与 GNOME 50 新增的 VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) 有关。
signals.review_reason: 单条 issue 但影响严重：界面冻结 1.5 秒以上直接阻断编辑主流程，而 XWayland 变通方案体验质量显著下降。这是 Linux/Wayland 用户的主要使用场景，影响日常编辑体验。

source_issues.title: Sluggishness in GNOME 50 / Wayland
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 AMD Radeon 780M + GNOME 50 + Wayland 上报告界面严重变慢，文件切换或滚动时出现 1.5 秒以上的冻结。运行 WAYLAND_DISPLAY="" (XWayland) 可以规避问题。日志无明确错误，怀疑与 GNOME 50 VRR 帧回调有关。
